Why:
  Understanding a document's full lifecycle — what happened, what
  checks ran, what's outstanding — currently means checking the Field
  Comparison table, the Authenticity/Anomaly pages, the Send Back

  at-a-glance traceability without visiting multiple pages, and without
  touching a single line of the extraction/matching/authenticity/
  anomaly/send-back engines it summarizes.

      for documentation parity). Polymorphic association design:
      parent_type/child_type ('invoice'|'po'|'gr') + parent_id/child_id
      (meaning documents.document_id / purchase_orders.po_id /
      goods_receipts.gr_id depending on type) — chosen because
      purchase_orders/goods_receipts rows have no independent row in
      `documents`, so a literal single-table FOREIGN KEY to
      `documents` can't express a PO or GR endpoint. CHECK constraints
      enforce valid types, that relationship_type matches its
      parent/child type pair, and no self-links; a UNIQUE constraint
      prevents duplicate relationships. Referential integrity for the
      polymorphic parent_id/child_id is enforced in the service layer
      (below), not the database, since Postgres FKs can't target three
      different tables from one column.
    - helpers/document_relationships.py (new): create_relationship(),
      delete_relationship(), get_relationship_by_id(),

      document_relationships first, and fall back to the legacy
      one-to-one attachment (purchase_orders.document_id /
      goods_receipts.document_id, mirroring routes/auditor.py::
      _build_comparison()'s own PO/GR selection) whenever a document

Risk assessment:
  - LOW risk to existing functionality: every change is additive (new
    table, new files, appended lines only); the matching engine, AI
    assistants, authenticity/anomaly engines, and every existing page
    are proven untouched via git diff and the full regression suite.
  - MEDIUM, documented trade-off: parent_id/child_id are polymorphic,
    so they cannot carry a real SQL FOREIGN KEY (Postgres FKs target
    exactly one table). Entity-existence validation happens in
    helpers/document_relationships.py::create_relationship() instead
    of the database — a direct INSERT bypassing this service layer
    (e.g. a future script, an admin tool) could create a dangling
    reference. Mitigated by: CHECK constraints on type validity/type-
    pair consistency, a UNIQUE constraint against duplicates, and the
    fact that this table currently has exactly one write path (the new
    API/service layer) with no other code touching it yet.
  - LOW risk from the legacy-fallback design: get_related_purchase_
    orders/goods_receipts/invoices() silently fall back to the old
    one-to-one attachment when no explicit relationship exists. This
    is intentional (STEP 4 compatibility requirement) but means a
    caller can't currently distinguish "no relationship data at all"
    from "using the legacy single attachment" except by checking
    whether relationship=None on the returned row.
  - No risk to AI cost/behavior: zero new Claude/Gemini calls.

Why it was changed:
  Phase 2 of the Enterprise V3 upgrade (Phase 1 built the underlying
  document_relationships table and service layer) — teaches AuditLens
  to understand and calculate multi-PO/multi-invoice/multi-GR
  relationships: partial invoicing, partial receipt, cumulative
  invoicing/receipt, remaining PO quantity/amount, over-invoicing,
  over-receipt, and duplicate-allocation prevention — while the
  existing one-to-one production workflow (Exception page, Report,
  Record Detail, AI Assistant, Workflow Timeline) keeps working exactly
  as before, completely unaware anything changed, until the new engine
  is explicitly turned on.

Relationship scoring rules:
  Every scorer gates on either an exact normalized PO-reference/PO-
  number match OR the legacy one-to-one document_id attachment first —
  a candidate with neither scores exactly 0 and is never created ("do
  not create a high-confidence relationship using vendor and amount
  alone"). From that gate, vendor match (+), vendor mismatch (-), item
  description match (+), quantity/amount plausibility against the
  counterpart (+/-), and date sequence validity (+/-) adjust the score,
  clamped to [0, 1]. MIN_AUTO_CONFIDENCE = 0.50 — below that, a
  candidate is never auto-created.

Allocation rules:
  matched_quantity/matched_amount on document_relationships are the
  allocation. A single qualifying PO candidate for an invoice gets the
  invoice's full quantity/amount; multiple qualifying PO candidates
  leave the allocation as None (ambiguous, never guessed) but still
  link every PO so it's discoverable. Cumulative PO totals sum every
  linked invoice's matched_quantity/matched_amount exactly once (a
  UNIQUE DB constraint already prevents a duplicate relationship row
  from existing at all). All arithmetic uses Decimal, never float.

Legacy fallback behavior:
  An invoice with zero explicit document_relationships rows is served
  entirely by the untouched _build_comparison() (build_comparison()
  short-circuits to it before even checking the feature flags' cost).
  Phase 1's get_related_purchase_orders/get_related_goods_receipts/
  get_related_invoices already fall back to the legacy one-to-one
  attachment when no explicit relationship exists, so even a request
  that does reach the V2 engine for a still-legacy invoice degrades
  gracefully to the same PO/GR legacy would have picked.

Feature-flag behavior:
  ENTERPRISE_MATCHING_V2_ENABLED=false, ENTERPRISE_MATCHING_V2_SHADOW_
  MODE=false by default (both). With both off, build_comparison() is a
  direct passthrough to _build_comparison() — no relationship lookup,
  no V2 code path, identical behavior and cost to before this phase
  existed. Shadow mode computes V2 alongside legacy purely for a
  concise DEBUG-level log line (never changes what's returned, never
  calls AI, never creates a duplicate exception). V2 enabled uses V2
  only for an invoice with explicit relationships, always with an
  exception-safe fallback to legacy.

API usage confirmation:
  Number of Claude calls added: 0. Number of Gemini calls added: 0. The
  entire matching engine (scoring, allocation, cumulative fulfilment)
  is deterministic field comparison and arithmetic — no LLM is called
  anywhere in helpers/relationship_builder.py or helpers/enterprise_
  matching.py, and none was added to anomaly detection's compatibility
  fix either.

Known limitations:
  - document_line_items has no po_id/gr_id column (only invoice
    document_id + a type tag), so line-item-level detail in V2's
    legacy-shaped keys is only available when the primary PO/GR is
    co-located under the invoice's own document_id — a genuinely
    cross-invoice-shared PO/GR gets line_items=[] (not computed) rather
    than a guessed/potentially-wrong comparison.
  - invoice_gr direct links are intentionally NOT created whenever
    another invoice also claims the same PO and there's more than one
    GR candidate (see the allocation rule above) — PO-level received
    totals are unaffected (they come from po_gr instead), but a
    per-invoice "matched_gr_count" in that specific situation falls
    back to "does the PO have any receipt evidence at all" rather than
    a direct per-invoice receipt record, since the schema has no way to
    express that distinction more precisely.
  - The relationship builder is not wired into the upload pipeline in
    this phase (routes/documents.py is completely untouched, by
    design, to keep the highest-risk file at zero risk) — relationships
    are built via the new backfill script or the existing Phase 1 API
    only. A future phase can add an opt-in, failure-isolated hook after
    extraction if desired.
  - Real Claude/Gemini interaction with this feature (e.g. whether the
    AI Assistant's prompts read naturally once V2 fields are exposed to
    it) has not been exercised with a live API key in this sandbox —
    no AI Assistant prompt/context changes were made in this phase at
    all, so no new interaction exists to verify.

      only replaced the old print block, no new query was introduced
      to the per-request dispatch path). _build_comparison() and
      _build_comparison_v2() themselves are byte-for-byte unchanged
      (confirmed via git diff — zero lines removed from either).
    - routes/document_relationships.py: added GET /documents/<id>/
      matching-comparison (STEP 4) — returns build_shadow_comparison()'s
      full structured result, working regardless of the current
      feature-flag state (so an auditor can inspect a comparison
      without needing shadow mode enabled first). New _require_auditor_
      only() access check — deliberately stricter than this file's
      existing _require_node_access() (which allows Finance for a
      document they own): the shadow-comparison debug endpoint excludes
      Finance entirely, since it's an internal engine-validation tool,
      not a document-review feature.
    - tests/extraction/test_shadow_comparison.py (new, 21 checks): the
      5 scenarios named by the task — (1) simple 1 PO/1 invoice/1 GR
      case where legacy and V2 agree with zero recorded differences;
      (2) the PO3006231-style 1 PO/2 invoices/2 GR case, verified live
      against the real dev DB — legacy reports FAIL (it can only ever
      compare an invoice's total against the PO's FULL amount, with no
      concept of "this invoice covers half the PO"), V2 correctly
      reports PASS, and a matching_status difference is recorded with a
      reason naming the actual cause ("Enterprise engine detected
      multiple related invoices") — a concrete demonstration of
      exactly the gap V2 exists to close; (3) an invoice with zero
      document_relationships rows resolves via the legacy fallback with
      no error and enterprise_v2/differences empty; (4) a genuinely
      multi-PO invoice is calculated correctly end-to-end through both
      _build_comparison_v2() directly and the shadow comparison; (5)
      every Claude/Gemini/AI-assistant call function is monkey-patched
      to raise if invoked, then shadow mode is run through both build_
      comparison() and build_shadow_comparison() — confirming neither
      code path ever touches an AI helper. Plus a pure (no DB) test
      that captures _log_shadow_comparison()'s actual stdout output and
      asserts a real amount value from the input never appears in it.
      Registered in tests/extraction/run_all.py.

  Untouched, verified via `git diff --stat`: routes/matching.py,
  routes/documents.py (OCR/upload pipeline), helpers/claude_extractor.py,
  helpers/gemini_extractor.py, helpers/anomaly_detector.py, helpers/
  authenticity_check.py, config.py (both feature flags already existed
  from Phase 2, still default false, no changes needed), every frontend
  file — zero lines changed in any of them.

Why it was changed:
  Phase 3 of the Enterprise V3 upgrade — before ENTERPRISE_MATCHING_V2_
  ENABLED can ever be safely flipped on in production, there needs to
  be a way to observe how the V2 engine's results would actually differ
  from the live legacy engine's results, on real data, with zero risk
  to what auditors currently see — shadow mode already existed
  structurally from Phase 2, but only produced a single unstructured
  debug print line with no way to inspect a specific comparison on
  demand. This phase makes that comparison a first-class, structured,
  safely-loggable object, and adds an on-demand debug endpoint so an
  auditor doesn't have to grep server logs to validate the engine.

Shadow flow diagram:
  Request for invoice X (any of: Record Detail comparison, Exception
  page, Report, AI Assistant, Workflow Timeline)
    -> routes/*.py calls build_comparison(cursor, X)
         -> both flags false (default): _build_comparison(X) -> return
            legacy result. [V2 code path never runs.]
         -> SHADOW_MODE=true: _build_comparison(X) -> legacy_result
                               (if X has document_relationships rows)
                               _build_comparison_v2(X) -> v2_result
                               _shape_shadow_comparison(...) -> comparison
                               _log_shadow_comparison(comparison) -> DEBUG log
                               return legacy_result  [ALWAYS legacy — the
                               response the browser receives is identical
                               to shadow mode being off.]
         -> V2_ENABLED=true (X has relationships): _build_comparison_v2(X)
                               -> v2_result, with an exception-safe
                               fallback to legacy_result if V2 raises.

  On-demand inspection (independent of the flags):
    Auditor calls GET /documents/<id>/matching-comparison
      -> _require_auditor_only() (Finance always 403, even for an owned doc)
      -> build_shadow_comparison(cursor, id) -> {legacy, enterprise_v2, differences}
      -> JSON response (never touches build_comparison()'s dispatch/flags)

Known limitations:
  - _log_shadow_comparison() only fires from build_comparison()'s
    dispatch path when SHADOW_MODE is actually enabled — with both
    flags at their default false, the new logging code exists but
    never executes on a live request, by design (shadow mode is opt-in
    diagnostics, not always-on overhead).
  - The debug endpoint (GET /documents/<id>/matching-comparison) always
    computes both engines live on each call (no caching) — acceptable
    at this app's current invoice volume (same reasoning already
    documented for /auditor/report/summary's own per-request
    recomputation), flagged for a real cache if volume grows.

Deployment instructions:
  1. Redeploy the Render BACKEND — no schema change, no new
     environment variables (both feature flags already existed from
     Phase 2 and keep their current values unless explicitly changed).
  2. No Render FRONTEND redeploy needed — zero frontend files changed.
  3. Recommended validation sequence before ever enabling V2: set
     ENTERPRISE_MATCHING_V2_SHADOW_MODE=true, watch Render logs for
     "DEBUG Matching Shadow Comparison" lines on invoices with
     document_relationships rows, and/or have an auditor hit GET
     /documents/<id>/matching-comparison directly for specific
     invoices of interest — legacy stays user-facing throughout. Only
     after that comparison looks correct, set ENTERPRISE_MATCHING_V2_
     ENABLED=true (per Phase 2's own deployment instructions).

Rollback instructions:
  Set ENTERPRISE_MATCHING_V2_SHADOW_MODE=false (already the default)
  and redeploy — the new logging/comparison code simply stops running
  on the dispatch path; the debug endpoint remains available (it's
  read-only and flag-independent) but can be ignored. No data was ever
  written by this phase, so there is nothing to clean up.

Both feature flags remain at their safe defaults after this phase:
  ENTERPRISE_MATCHING_V2_ENABLED=false
  ENTERPRISE_MATCHING_V2_SHADOW_MODE=false

Why it was changed:
  Phase 5 of the Enterprise V3 upgrade - Phases 1-4 built and wired the
  many-to-many matching engine, but Finance still uploaded every
  document independently with no way to express "these 5 documents are
  one AP transaction" before an auditor ever sees them. This phase adds
  that organizational layer for Finance, while leaving every matching/
  extraction/authenticity/anomaly engine exactly as Phases 1-4 left it -
  Enterprise Matching V2 discovers the grouped documents' relationships
  itself (via the same deterministic, already-existing relationship
  builder now simply triggered a bit earlier, at grouping time instead
  of only on-demand), never duplicated or reimplemented here.

Database changes:
  2 new additive tables (transaction_packages, transaction_package_
  documents) - see the detail above. No column added to, no constraint
  changed on, any existing table.

New routes:
  Backend: POST /transaction-packages, GET /transaction-packages, GET
  /transaction-packages/<id>, POST /transaction-packages/<id>/documents.
  Frontend: /finance/transactions, /finance/transactions/create,
  /finance/transactions/detail?id=X.

Upload flow diagram:
  Mode 1 (existing, completely unchanged):
    Finance uploads ONE document
      -> POST /documents/upload (or upload-po/upload-gr/<id>)
      -> existing OCR + Claude/Gemini extraction
      -> Finance Correction / Auditor review, exactly as before

  Mode 2 (new, this phase):
    Finance selects files for Purchase Orders / Invoices / Goods
    Receipts on /finance/transactions/create
      -> POST /transaction-packages (create the package row)
      -> for each Invoice file: POST /documents/upload (EXISTING,
         unmodified) -> document_id
      -> for each PO/GR file (only once >=1 invoice exists in the
         package): POST /documents/upload-po|gr/<first_invoice_id>
         (EXISTING, unmodified) -> po_id / gr_id
      -> for each uploaded document: POST /transaction-packages/<id>/
         documents { document_id, document_role }
           -> link_document_to_package() validates + inserts, then
              calls the EXISTING build_relationships_for_invoice() for
              every invoice in the package (Phase 2, untouched)
           -> compute_package_status() recomputes 'waiting_documents' /
              'processing' / 'completed'
      -> Enterprise Matching V2 (Phase 2/4, untouched) picks up the new
         document_relationships rows automatically the next time
         anyone views any linked invoice - no separate "run matching"
         step needed
      -> Auditor Review - Record Detail, Exceptions, Report, AI
         Assistant, Workflow Timeline (Phase 4) all already read
         through the same build_comparison() dispatcher, unaware
         (and not needing to be aware) that these documents arrived via
         a package instead of independently

Known limitations:

    invoices in its package (a real constraint of the existing upload-

      comparison_v2() already computes the correct allocation-aware
      invoice_result (a partial-fulfilment invoice correctly resolves

      already routed through _matching_status_for_comparison() to
      correct for exactly this (that function's own docstring cites
      "the PO3006231 example") - Record Detail was the one consumer
      that never got the fix. No new matching calculation: reuses the
      exact function every other consumer already trusts, and is a
      no-op for legacy (non-V2) comparisons.
    - routes/authenticity.py: both GET /authenticity (list) and GET
      /authenticity/<id> (detail) now include transaction_context per
      row, added inside the one shared per-row enrichment function
      (_with_authentication_score) both endpoints already call. New
      _transaction_context_for_row() reuses get_transaction_context_for_
      document() (Phase 6) unchanged, translating document_type ('po'/
      'gr') plus the row's own po_id/gr_id into the (document_role,
      document_id) shape that function expects - authenticity_checks
      keys PO/GR rows by the invoice document_id they were uploaded
      alongside, while transaction_package_documents links PO/GR by
      po_id/gr_id (the same distinction already handled by Phase 6's
      get_transaction_authenticity_summary host_document_id fix).

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/):
    - auditor-record-detail.component.ts/html: the Amount row and Line
      Items table are computed client-side and were still comparing a

      allocation existed, independent of the backend's verdict. Fixed
      via a new isV2Allocated/amountCompareBasis getter (uses invoice_
      result.allocated_amount, already computed and returned by the
      backend - no new calculation) and an isPartialAllocationLineItem()
      check that renders a neutral "Partial Allocation" pill instead of
      a hard "Mismatch" when a PO-side line-item quantity difference is
      explained by a correct multi-invoice allocation (V2's own invoice_
      result.status === 'PASS' and the invoice never bills more than the
      PO line - a genuine over-invoice still shows as a mismatch).
    - auditor-record-detail.component.ts: normalizeVendor() was
      stripping punctuation to nothing instead of a space, unlike the
      backend's helpers/entity_normalizer.py (which the backend's real,
      already-correct match_result.vendor_match already uses). This
      turned "A.Waner" into "awaner" while "A WANER" stayed "a waner" -
      two names the backend already treats as identical, rendered as
      "Differ" on this row's independent client-side pill. Fixed to

    - auditor-record-detail.component.html/css: the "Transaction

    - auditor/shared/authenticity-evidence.util.ts (NEW): both the
      Authenticity list page and detail page already read the SAME
      authenticity_checks row, but interpreted it with two independently
      -written rules - the list page showed raw has_company_logo/has_
      signature booleans as a strict yes/no badge with no awareness of

    - auditor-authenticity.component.ts/html/css: removed the dominant,

    - auditor-authenticity-detail.component.ts: documentEvidenceRows now

Date: 2026-07-23
What was changed:
  Two workflow bugs found after Phase 7, traced to a single upstream
  root cause: transaction package membership had no protection against
  the same real invoice being linked into two different packages.

  Backend (auditlens-backend/):
    - helpers/transaction_packages.py: link_document_to_package() only
      ever checked whether a document was already linked to the SAME
      package - nothing prevented it from also being linked into a
      DIFFERENT package. New find_existing_package_for_invoice()
      matches an invoice against every OTHER package's invoices by
      invoice_number (normalized-exact) + vendor (existing fuzzy is_
      same_company()) + amount (existing AMOUNT_TOLERANCE) + invoice_
      date (3-day tolerance) - all four must agree, deliberately strict
      so two genuinely different invoices are never blocked. When
      linking a document with document_role='invoice', a match in a
      different package now returns a clear error identifying that
      package instead of silently creating a fragmented duplicate
      grouping. No new matching engine: reuses the exact vendor/amount
      comparators already trusted elsewhere in this app.

Why:
  Fixed matching calculation caused false mismatch in Record Detail
  comparison using allocation-aware matching. The Phase 7 fix (compare
  against Enterprise V2's allocated_amount instead of the PO's full
  total) only engages when engine_version === 'v2', which requires the
  invoice to have document_relationships rows. _rebuild_relationships_
  for_package() only ever runs the relationship builder for invoices
  that are members of THAT specific package - so an invoice fragmented
  into a second, PO/GR-less package (nothing previously stopped this)
  never gets a chance to link to its real PO/GR, engine_version stays
  legacy for it, and Record Detail falls back to the old single-invoice-
  vs-full-PO comparison regardless of the Phase 7 display fix already
  being correct. Root cause traced to duplicate invoice transaction
  creation causing incorrect "Missing PO and GR": with the membership
  guard in place, an invoice can no longer be split across two
  packages, so this class of false mismatch can no longer occur going
  forward. Improved transaction grouping consistency: one invoice now
  belongs to exactly one transaction package, enforced at link time.

  helpers/relationship_builder.py and helpers/enterprise_matching.py
  were read to confirm they already handle multiple sibling invoices
  sharing one PO correctly (each gets its own full allocation against a
  single matching PO candidate) - neither needed a change; the gap was
  entirely in package membership, not matching calculation.

  - python tests/extraction/run_all.py - all 25 suites pass, including
    test_transaction_packages.py (existing single-invoice-per-package
    linking scenarios still pass unaffected by the new guard).
  - Live smoke test against the real local Postgres dev DB (rows

  Claude calls: 0. Gemini calls: 0.

  This fix is preventive - it stops the duplicate-package scenario

Date: 2026-07-23
What was changed:
  Phase 10: fixed "Object of type memoryview is not JSON serializable"
  on Record Detail's Open button.

  Root cause (confirmed by reproducing with real bytea content, not
  assumed): helpers/document_relationships.py's get_related_purchase_
  orders(), get_related_goods_receipts(), and get_related_invoices()
  each ran a bare SELECT * (or documents d.*) against purchase_orders/
  goods_receipts/documents - all three of which have a file_bytes BYTEA
  column (the durable, DB-stored copy of the original uploaded file,
  used because Render's disk is ephemeral). psycopg2 returns a BYTEA
  value as a Python memoryview, which Flask's jsonify() cannot
  serialize. These three functions are called directly by _build_
  comparison_v2() (routes/auditor.py) and their raw output is returned
  verbatim as related_purchase_orders/related_invoices/related_goods_
  receipts in GET /auditor/record/<id>/comparison's JSON response -
  the exact endpoint Record Detail's Open button loads.

  This bug is NOT new - it has existed in helpers/document_
  relationships.py since Phase 1, before this session's work began.
  It stayed silently dormant because Enterprise Matching V2 (which is
  the only code path that calls these three functions) wasn't
  successfully engaging until Phase 9.1/the user's own environment fix
  - the moment V2 started actually running, this pre-existing leak
  surfaced for the first time.

  The rest of this codebase already handles this correctly in every
  other place BYTEA columns get read for a JSON response (routes/
  documents.py's get_po_list/get_gr_list/get_supporting_documents all
  explicitly `row.pop('file_bytes', None)`) - document_relationships.py
  was the one place that had never been audited for it, since its
  SELECT * queries predate the file_bytes column's introduction.

  Backend (auditlens-backend/):
    - helpers/document_relationships.py: all 6 SELECT sites across the
      three functions now strip file_bytes from the returned dict
      before it's used, matching the exact convention already
      established in routes/documents.py. No other columns touched -
      every other metadata field (file_name, file_type, vendor_name,
      amounts, etc.) is preserved exactly as before. The actual file
      content remains available exactly as before, through the
      existing, unmodified file-serving endpoints (GET /documents/
      <id>/file, /documents/po/<po_id>/file, /documents/gr/<gr_id>/
      file) - nothing about file download/view changed.

Why:
  Auditors could not open a Record Detail page for any invoice whose
  Enterprise Matching V2 relationships included a PO/GR/sibling invoice
  with its file bytes stored in the database (i.e. essentially every
  real uploaded document) - the comparison API 500'd before any data
  reached the page.

  enterprise_matching.py and relationship_builder.py were not touched -
  this was purely a JSON-serialization bug in how already-fetched
  rows were shaped for the API response, not a matching calculation
  issue. OCR, Claude/Gemini extraction, and the authenticity engine
  were not touched either.

Test results:
  - python tests/extraction/run_all.py - all 25 suites pass, including
    test_document_relationships.py (no regression in the existing

  - Live smoke test against the real local Postgres dev DB, this time

Date: 2026-07-23
What was changed:
  Phase 12: fixed a false red "Mismatch" on the GR column of a Line
  Items row that was already correctly matched, and the row's red
  background persisting even when the invoice's overall matching
  status was PASS.

  Root cause (confirmed by tracing the exact rendering logic): the GR
  column's pill/icon/text (auditor-record-detail.component.ts) read
  li.quantity_match — a single BLENDED 3-way flag ("are invoice, PO,
  and GR quantities ALL equal at once") — instead of comparing the
  invoice's quantity against the GR's OWN quantity specifically. For
  the real PO3006231 case, invoice=15000 and GR=15000 (an exact match),
  but PO=30000 (a correct partial allocation, already softened for the
  PO column in Phase 11/8) made the BLENDED flag false, and that false
  value leaked into the GR column's pill even though GR and invoice
  agreed perfectly. The row's red background had the same root cause
  one level up: it fell back to a plain row-mismatch class whenever
  li.amount_match was false, without checking whether that too was
  just the PO's full amount vs the invoice's allocated share (already
  known to be a valid allocation from the Amount row directly above it
  in the same page).

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/):
    - auditor-record-detail.component.ts: new lineItemSideQuantityMatch
      (li, side) does a genuine PAIRWISE comparison (invoice vs THIS
      side's own quantity only) instead of relying on the blended flag.
      lineItemPillClass/Icon/Text and lineItemRowClass now use this for
      both the PO and GR columns (the PO column keeps its existing
      allocation-aware override from Phase 8/11 layered on top - a PO
      quantity difference explained by a valid partial allocation still
      shows Match). lineItemRowClass also no longer shows a red
      background for a soft amount_match difference when V2's own
      invoice_result already confirmed this row is a correct allocation
      - the SAME reasoning already applied to quantity. lineItemPo
      DisplayQuantity's allocation-detection condition was updated to
      match (a small new showPoAllocationContext() helper, replacing a
      duplicated inline condition in the template).

Why:
  A completely genuine GR match (15000 received == 15000 invoiced) was
  showing as a hard "Mismatch" purely because an unrelated column's
  (the PO's) raw, un-allocated total happened to differ - a false
  signal an auditor could easily misread as "goods weren't fully
  received," when in fact the goods receipt was exactly correct. The
  row's persistent red background compounded this: once every

Date: 2026-07-23
What was changed:
  Phase 15: added a Delete management feature for Transaction Packages
  (Finance's Transaction Packages page).

  Backend (auditlens-backend/):
    - helpers/transaction_packages.py: new delete_package(package_id) -
      deletes a package and every document EXCLUSIVELY owned by it. A
      document also linked to a DIFFERENT package (checked per
      (document_role, document_id) pair via transaction_package_
      documents) is left completely untouched - only this package's
      own membership link disappears. Also accounts for the legacy
      "co-located" PO/GR case (purchase_orders/goods_receipts.
      document_id -> documents is ON DELETE NO ACTION, not CASCADE, so
      an un-linked co-located PO/GR would otherwise block deleting its
      host invoice) - unless that co-located PO/GR is itself
      independently linked to a different package, in which case the
      invoice is left untouched too rather than risking an incorrect
      delete. Every statement runs on ONE transaction (commits only
      once every delete has succeeded; any failure rolls back the
      entire operation, so a package can never be left half-deleted).
      No matching/relationship CALCULATION logic is touched anywhere -
      every delete is a plain row removal of already-computed data, in
      FK-safe order (verified against the actual live schema's FK
      constraints before writing a single line).
    - routes/transaction_packages.py: new DELETE /transaction-packages/
      <id>/force route (Finance-only, package-owner-only) calling
      delete_package(). Deliberately a SEPARATE route from the existing
      DELETE /transaction-packages/<id> (which stays completely
      unmodified) - that route is called automatically and silently by
      the create-package flow to clean up an empty "ghost" package
      (Phase 9) and must keep refusing anything non-empty; this new
      route is the explicit, user-confirmed "delete everything" action,
      only ever reachable from a confirmation modal.

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/):
    - finance-transactions.component.ts/html/css: added a Delete button
      beside the existing Open button in the Transaction Packages
      table, and a confirmation modal ("Delete this transaction package
      and all related documents? This action cannot be undone.") before
      calling the new endpoint. On success: the package list refreshes
      automatically and a success message is shown; on failure, the
      error is shown inside the modal without closing it.

Why:
  Gives Finance a way to remove a transaction package (e.g. one created
  by mistake, or a test/duplicate) along with its documents, without
  needing direct database access - while guaranteeing a document shared
  with another package (Phase 7.1 explicitly allows this) is never
  deleted out from under that other package.

  helpers/relationship_builder.py, helpers/enterprise_matching.py, OCR
  extraction, Claude/Gemini extraction, and the authenticity engine
  were not touched. Transaction package CREATION logic, auto-grouping
  logic (resolve_package_for_document), and document LINKING logic
  (link_document_to_package) are all completely unmodified - this
  phase only adds a new deletion path alongside them.

Test results:
  - python tests/extraction/run_all.py - all 25 suites pass, including
    test_transaction_packages.py (existing package creation/linking
    behavior unaffected).
  - Live smoke test against the real local Postgres dev DB (rows
    created and cleaned up), covering every requirement explicitly:
    (1) deleted Package A (PO3006231, 2 invoices, 2 GRs, all
    exclusively owned) via the real DELETE .../force endpoint - package
    disappears from the list, and all 5 documents are confirmed gone
    from documents/purchase_orders/goods_receipts; (2) a completely
    separate Package B (unrelated invoice) is confirmed untouched -
    still listed, its document still in the DB; (3) an invoice
    deliberately linked into BOTH Package C and Package D - deleting
    Package C reports 0 deleted invoices / 1 kept-shared-document, the
    shared invoice is confirmed still in the DB, and Package D still
    shows it - the safety rule holds. Package C itself was still
    correctly removed from the list.
  - npx ng build --configuration production - succeeded (exit 0; same
    pre-existing bundle-size warnings, no new errors).

Build result:
  Backend: all 25 test suites pass. Frontend: clean production build,
  exit 0.

  Claude calls: 0. Gemini calls: 0.

Date: 2026-07-23
What was changed:
  Phase 18: expanded the existing Admin module (seeded admin account,
  Admin dashboard, admin API from a prior phase) with User Management
  and Document Management, per the Admin module spec. Purely additive
  to that module; two small, disclosed exceptions to the "do not
  touch" list were required and are called out below.

  Backend (auditlens-backend/routes/admin.py, all new, all role=='admin'
  gated, 403 otherwise):
    - DELETE /admin/users/<id> - safe deletion. Users are referenced
      (NO ACTION, no CASCADE) from 13 different FK relationships
      (documents, purchase_orders, goods_receipts, review_records,
      send_back_cycles, anomalies, calendar_tasks, transaction_
      packages, audit_logs). Rather than hand-checking each one, the
      DELETE is attempted and a ForeignKeyViolation is caught and
      turned into a 409 with a clear message ("...disable the account
      instead") - covers all 13 relationships automatically, can't go
      stale if a future table adds its own FK to users, and documents
      are never cascade-deleted. Self-delete is blocked, same pattern
      as the existing self-deactivate guard.
    - POST /admin/users/<id>/reset-password - admin sets a temporary
      password (min 6 chars), hashed with the exact same bcrypt call
      routes/auth.py's own register()/login() already use.
    - GET /admin/documents (existing endpoint, enriched) - each row now
      also carries document_number (invoice_number, falling back to
      file_name) and document_type ('invoice'). These rows are always
      invoices - purchase_orders/goods_receipts have no status column
      of their own in this schema, so they remain visible via the
      existing Record Detail related-documents view rather than as
      separate top-level rows here.
    - POST /admin/documents/<id>/approve, POST /admin/documents/<id>/
      send-back ({target: 'finance'|'auditor', reason, message}) -
      admin-only oversight actions. Deliberately separate endpoints
      from Auditor's own POST /reviews/approve and POST /reviews/return
      (routes/reviews.py, completely untouched) rather than broadening
      their role check - they reuse the exact same documents.status /
      review_records / send_back_cycles transitions those already
      perform. "Send back to auditor" (documents.status -> 'under_
      review', which is what already puts a case back in the Auditor's
      own GET /reviews/queue) has no matching review_records.action in
      that table's existing CHECK constraint (approved/returned/
      resubmitted/closed all mean something else), so it's recorded via
      the general-purpose audit_logs trail instead of review_records,
      without altering that constraint.

  Two disclosed, minimal exceptions to "do not touch" (routes/
  auditor.py, routes/authenticity.py): the spec requires Admin to view
  OCR/authenticity/matching results by reusing the existing Record
  Detail page, and forbids duplicating the matching logic to build a
  second view. The two read-only GET endpoints that page depends on
  (GET /auditor/record/<id>/comparison, GET /authenticity/<id>) were
  hard-gated role=='auditor' only - an admin JWT got a flat 403, so
  Record Detail would have loaded empty for Admin. Both guards were
  widened by one line each, from role != 'auditor' to role not in
  ('auditor', 'admin'). No matching/authenticity computation logic was
  touched - build_comparison()/run_authenticity_check() and every other
  route in both files are unchanged, and Auditor's own access is
  provably unaffected (see test results below).

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/):
    - admin/users/ (new) - User Management page (/admin/users): table
      of User ID / Full Name / Email / Role / Status / Created Date /
      Actions; Disable/Enable (existing PUT /admin/users/<id>/status,
      unchanged), Reset Password (modal), Delete (confirmation modal,
      surfaces the 409 safe-deletion message verbatim). Self-actions
      disabled on the admin's own row.
    - admin/documents/ (new) - Document Management page (/admin/
      documents): table of Document Number / Vendor / Document Type /

  Existing deletion logic found (inspected before writing anything new,

    - routes/documents.py::delete_document() (DELETE /documents/<id>,
      Finance-only) - a basic, pre-transaction-package-era delete. Left

      was not reused as-is.
    - helpers/transaction_packages.py::delete_package() (Phase 15,
      transaction package force-delete) - THIS is the safe-deletion
      pattern that was actually reused: FK-safe explicit deletion order
      for the NO ACTION children, explicit document_relationships
      cleanup (polymorphic, no real FK), reliance on documents' own ON
      DELETE CASCADE for ai_assistant_cache/anomalies/authenticity_
      checks/document_line_items/send_back_cycles, one DB transaction
      with rollback on any failure, and the "never delete a document
      shared with another package" check via the existing
      _is_linked_to_other_package() helper.

  Backend:
    - helpers/transaction_packages.py - new delete_single_document()
      (+ DocumentProtectedError), added directly below delete_package()
      and reusing its private helpers (_is_linked_to_other_package,
      _recompute_and_persist_status, _rebuild_relationships_for_
      package) unmodified. Deletes ONE invoice-role document
      (documents.document_id) and its exclusively-owned children:
      extracted_fields, exceptions, record_matches, three_way_matches,
      review_records (NO ACTION children, deleted explicitly);
      document_relationships (polymorphic, deleted explicitly); this
      document's own transaction_package_documents membership link
      only (the package and every OTHER document in it are untouched);
      a co-located Purchase Order/Goods Receipt (purchase_orders.
      document_id / goods_receipts.document_id, uploaded alongside this
      invoice) if it isn't linked to any transaction package itself.
      ai_assistant_cache/anomalies/authenticity_checks/document_line_
      items/send_back_cycles are removed automatically via documents'
      existing ON DELETE CASCADE - not touched explicitly.
      claude_extraction_cache/gemini_extraction_cache/authenticity_
      result_cache are content-hash-keyed (not document-specific,
      shared across any file with identical bytes) and are correctly
      never touched. One DB transaction throughout: commits only after
      every delete succeeds, rolls back on any failure.

      Safety rule for a co-located PO/GR that IS linked to a
      transaction package: purchase_orders.document_id/goods_receipts.
      document_id turned out to be nullable at the schema level (not
      NOT NULL, as initially assumed - checked directly against
      pg_constraint before writing this), so a "detach" (set document_
      id = NULL) would have been schema-legal. Deliberately not done:
      that would leave a real PO/GR row in a document_id=NULL state
      neither Enterprise Matching V2 nor relationship_builder.py has
      ever been written or tested against, and both are explicitly out
      of scope to risk here. The whole deletion is rejected instead,
      with a clear message naming the specific PO/GR and pointing at
      the package - every row is left exactly as it was, satisfying
      the "reject deletion with a clear message" option the task itself
      offered as an alternative to detaching.
    - routes/admin.py - new DELETE /admin/documents/<id> (admin-only,
      403 for every other role) calling delete_single_document():
      ValueError -> 404, DocumentProtectedError -> 409, success -> 200
      with counts of any co-deleted PO/GR. No binary file data (file_
      bytes) is read or returned anywhere in the response.

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/src/app/admin/documents/):
    - Red-outline Delete button added beside the existing View button.
    - Confirmation modal: "Delete Document?" / the exact required
      message / document number, vendor, document type / Cancel +
      Delete Document buttons.
    - On success: modal closes, a "Document deleted successfully."
      toast appears (auto-dismisses after 3s), and the document is
      removed from the already-fetched local array - the table and the
      filter-chip summary counts (both computed from that same array
      via getters) update immediately with no page reload and no extra
      network round-trip.
    - On failure: the backend's error message (e.g. the 409 protected-
      document message) is shown inside the still-open modal.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Date: 2026-07-24
What was changed:
  Phase 24: pure sizing/spacing refinement of Auditor Home's chart
  section - no structural, functional, or data changes. HTML file was
  not touched at all; only CSS values and Chart.js style options
  (legend padding/font sizes, point sizes) in the 2 files below.

  Root cause found and fixed: the previous phase's chart-height
  reductions (.chart-body/.chart-body-small) had little visible
  effect, because .chart-body used flex: 1 inside .chart-card's flex
  column. CSS Grid's default align-items: stretch made every card in
  a chart row match the row's tallest card, and flex: 1 then made the
  canvas area GROW to consume all of that stretched extra space -
  silently overriding the explicit height value. Fixed by changing
  .chart-body to flex: 0 0 auto (fixed size, no grow/shrink) and
  giving .chart-card explicit align-items: stretch; justify-content:
  flex-start, so leftover space (if any) collects visibly at the
  bottom of a card instead of invisibly inflating the chart canvas.

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/src/app/auditor/dashboard/):
    - .chart-body (Audit Trend, Review Volume): 130px -> 100px, and

Date: 2026-07-25
What was changed:
  Phase 36: fixed Finance Home's Document Processing Queue so invoices
  that share the same linked PO (i.e. belong to the same procurement/
  AP case) are grouped into ONE row instead of appearing as duplicate
  separate rows. Frontend only — no backend, no database changes.

  Reported bug: two invoices (e.g. L000016639 and L000016545) sharing
  one PO were shown as two unrelated rows in the queue, even though
  the previous phase's Related Docs column already cross-referenced
  them textually within each row — the ROWS themselves were still not
  merged.

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/src/app/finance/home/):
    - finance-home.component.ts: replaced the previous phase's flat
      "documents = thisMonthDocs.slice(0, 5)" (one row per invoice)
      plus its 3 per-row Related Docs helpers (relatedInvoiceNumbers/
      relatedPoLabel/relatedGrLabel, now dead code) with a single
      computeQueueGroups() method and a new `queueRows` field:
      - Groups this month's invoices by their linked PO number (via
        the SAME poList/grList already loaded by loadPoGrLists() —
        no new request); an invoice with no PO stays its own
        single-member group rather than being merged with anything.
      - Each group becomes one row: Document/Related Docs show every
        member invoice's number joined together; PO shows the shared
        PO number; GR shows the UNION of every member's own GR
        number(s) (deduplicated).
      - The other columns (Status/Required Action/Age/Action) need a
        single representative value per group: Status/Required
        Action/Action are taken from the group's most URGENT member
        (priority order: returned > under_review/resubmitted >
        ocr_processing > ocr_done > approved), so a case isn't hidden
        behind an already-approved sibling; OCR Confidence is the
        group's average; Age uses the OLDEST member (most
        conservative/urgent framing); Vendor is read straight from
        the representative member (a shared PO is inherently one
        vendor).
      - Same dual call-site pattern already used elsewhere on this
        page (e.g. computeCorrectionAnalysis()): computeQueueGroups()
        is called from both loadDocuments() and loadPoGrLists(), so
        whichever of the two async loads finishes last is the one
        that actually produces populated grouped rows.
    - finance-home.component.html: table body now iterates
      `queueRows` instead of raw `documents`; every existing column's
      binding was updated to read from the grouped row shape (e.g.
      requiredActionLabel(row.primaryDoc), onAction(row.primaryDoc))
      rather than removed - Status/OCR Confidence/Required Action/
      Action all still call the EXACT SAME existing methods as
      before, just against the group's representative document.
    - finance-home.component.css: Related Docs cell changed from
      single-line ellipsis truncation to wrapping text (a grouped
      row's comma-joined invoice/GR list can be longer than a single
      reference number, and truncating it would hide exactly the
      relationship this column exists to show); column widths
      rebalanced to give Related Docs more room.

Why:
  The auditor/finance side already understands "these 2 invoices are
  the same AP case" once a shared PO makes that clear - showing them
  as 2 separate queue rows was misleading and made the queue look
  like there were more open items than there actually are.

Date: 2026-07-25
What was changed:
  Phase 37: tightened Finance Home's Document Processing Queue grouping
  (added in the previous phase) to prevent a real over-grouping risk —
  invoices from DIFFERENT vendors could be incorrectly merged into one
  row if their PO numbers happened to be textually identical (e.g. a
  generic/reused PO numbering scheme, or an OCR misread). Frontend
  only — no backend, no database changes.

  auditlens-frontend/src/app/finance/home/finance-home.component.ts,
  computeQueueGroups():
    - Grouping key changed from PO NUMBER TEXT ALONE to PO NUMBER +
      VENDOR (both normalized via trim + lowercase before comparing,
      to tolerate minor OCR/formatting whitespace-or-case
      differences without loosening the match into a false positive).
      A genuine procurement case is a specific vendor billing against
      a specific PO — matching on the PO string in isolation was too
      permissive.
    - Behavior for the actual reported case is unchanged: two
      invoices that share BOTH the same PO number and the same
      vendor (a real shared-PO procurement case) still merge into one
      row exactly as before, with the same PO-shown-once / GR-union /
      most-urgent-status aggregation logic untouched.
    - New protection: two invoices that share only a coincidentally-
      matching PO number STRING but belong to DIFFERENT vendors no
      longer merge — each stays its own row, since they are not
      actually the same procurement case.
    - Everything else in computeQueueGroups() (the poGrLoaded guard,
      the dual call-site pattern with loadDocuments()/loadPoGrLists(),
      the ungrouped-when-no-PO fallback, the GR union, the STATUS_
      PRIORITY-based representative document) is unchanged — only the
      grouping key itself and the local variable it's built from
      (renamed poByDocId, now storing {number, vendor} instead of a
      bare string) changed.

Why:
  Follow-up correction: the previous phase's grouping only checked
  matching PO number text, which risked incorrectly combining
  unrelated invoices into one row whenever two different vendors'
  invoices happened to reference a similarly-formatted or coincidentally
  identical PO number - undermining the very "one row per real AP case"
  goal the feature exists for. Requested fix: only merge invoices that
  truly belong to the same procurement case.

Date: 2026-07-25
What was changed:
  Phase 38: replaced Finance Home's Document Processing Queue grouping
  with the SAME grouping mechanism Auditor Home's Transaction Review
  Queue actually uses — real transaction_package membership — instead
  of the previous phase's PO-number/vendor TEXT-matching heuristic.
  Frontend only — no backend, no database changes, no Auditor files
  touched.

  Also checked (before writing any code) whether this was actually a
  deployment gap rather than a code bug: this repo's own render.yaml
  configures both services as standard Render Blueprint web services
  with no `autoDeploy: false`, so Render auto-deploys on every push to
  main - there is no separate manual "update Render" action available
  to trigger from here. Per the project's standing update-workflow
  preference, this is noted explicitly below rather than silently
  assumed handled.

  Why the previous (PO+vendor) fix was still insufficient: it was a
  heuristic INFERRING a relationship from matching text fields, which
  is a fundamentally different (and less trustworthy) signal than
  Auditor Home's actual grouping, which groups by literal
  transaction_package_documents membership - an explicit, Finance-
  created relationship, not inferred from text. Two invoices could
  share matching PO text without being formally linked into the same
  case (or vice versa, in principle), so a heuristic can never fully
  "match Auditor's grouping behavior" - only reading the same
  relationship data Auditor reads can.

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/src/app/finance/home/finance-home.
  component.ts):
    - New loadTransactionPackages(): calls the EXISTING GET
      /transaction-packages (Finance-scoped list, already used by
      finance-transactions.component.ts) then, for every package
      returned, GET /transaction-packages/<id> (existing detail
      endpoint) in parallel via forkJoin - the same forkJoin-over-a-
      bounded-set pattern already used by loadCyclesForActionStats()
      in this file. Both endpoints already existed and were already
      used elsewhere in this app; neither routes/transaction_
      packages.py nor helpers/transaction_packages.py were touched.
      Builds packageGroupByDocId: a Map from each package-linked
      invoice's document_id to that package's combined, deduplicated
      invoice/PO/GR numbers (read from get_package_documents() output
      - the SAME helper function Auditor's list_all_packages_with_
      documents() calls internally for its own queue).
    - computeQueueGroups() rewritten: an invoice found in

      as a mismatch even when that invoice's own allocated share
      genuinely matches — using the same corrected basis here means
      this new section can never show a variance that contradicts the
      Field Comparison table directly below it. No new API call —
      every value (`comparison.invoice.total_amount`, `comparison.po`,
      `amountCompareBasis`) was already loaded on this page for that
      same table. Returns null (section hidden) when there's no invoice
      amount to report, or when the exception has no real financial
      angle (amounts match, no PO/GR missing) — nothing is fabricated.

What was changed:
  Phase 43: added a 5th AI Audit Assistant action, "Approval
  Assessment", answering the 4 approval-readiness questions the task
  named — is this ready for approval, what unresolved issues prevent
  it, what evidence/documents are required, what checks should the
  auditor complete first — using the SAME context/validation/API
  infrastructure the existing 4 actions already share. No separate AI
  module, no new AI provider, no schema change.

  Root cause / design note (inspected before writing code): every
  existing action already goes through ONE shared pipeline —
  routes/ai_assistant.py::_build_case_context() (assembles matching/
  missing-docs/authenticity/anomalies/audit_status once) ->
  _run_action() (cache lookup, calls ask_ai_assistant(), applies an
  action-specific clamp when one exists, saves to cache) ->
  helpers/ai_assistant.py::ask_ai_assistant() (Claude-primary/Gemini-
  fallback, one shared system preamble + one per-action instruction).
  Approval Assessment is implemented as one more entry in that SAME
  pipeline — a new _ACTION_INSTRUCTIONS key, a new _clamp_* function
  following the EXACT pattern _clamp_explain_exception_result already
  established, and one more route calling the SAME _run_action() every
  other endpoint calls. Nothing about the shared plumbing changed.

  auditlens-backend/routes/ai_assistant.py:
    - _build_case_context(): added ONE new field, 'po_amount' (the
      PO's own total_amount, already computed by build_comparison() —
      nothing new calculated), so the AI can cite concrete financial
      figures for Approval Assessment's "financial impact" dimension.
      Deliberately the raw PO total, not an allocation-aware figure —
      the pre-existing transaction_context.allocation_summary field
      (added in an earlier phase) already carries the correct allocated
      amount for a v2/enterprise package invoice, and the system
      preamble already tells the AI to defer to that when present, so
      this stays a plain, non-duplicated read rather than re-deriving
      the frontend's allocation-aware amountCompareBasis logic on the
      backend too (the task explicitly said not to create duplicate
      logic).
    - New _compute_approval_readiness(context): the DETERMINISTIC
      Ready / Not Ready / Requires Review verdict, computed in Python —
      never left for the AI to decide, the same guarantee
      _compute_audit_status/_clamp_explain_exception_result already
      give every other action. 'Ready' only when audit_status is
      already 'PASS'. Otherwise splits 'REVIEW REQUIRED' into 'Not
      Ready' (a missing document, a 'blocking' anomaly, an authenticity
      warning, or a hard FAIL-level matching mismatch — any of which
      genuinely blocks approval) vs 'Requires Review' (REVIEW REQUIRED
      but none of those hard blockers apply — a softer signal needing
      the auditor's own judgment, not a hard stop). Built entirely from
      fields _build_case_context() already computes.
    - New _clamp_approval_assessment_result(result, context): mirrors
      _clamp_explain_exception_result exactly — approval_readiness is
      ALWAYS the deterministic value above, never the AI's guess;
      blocking_factors is forced empty for a 'Ready' verdict regardless
      of what the AI said, and falls back to audit_status_reasons
      (already-trusted elsewhere) when the AI returns nothing usable;
      evidence/recommended_actions get safe non-empty defaults; every
      list is filtered to non-empty strings only (never crashes on a
      malformed/non-string AI entry).
    - _run_action(): one new elif branch applying the clamp above for
      action == 'approval_assessment' — identical shape to the existing
      prepare_send_back/explain_exception branches.
    - New route: POST /ai-assistant/<document_id>/approval-assessment
      — same _require_auditor() gate, same _run_action() call, same
      try/except-500 shape as every other auditor-facing endpoint in
      this file.

  auditlens-backend/helpers/ai_assistant.py:

Date: 2026-07-26
What was changed:
  Phase 46 (Performance Phase 1): added database connection pooling to
  auditlens-backend/db.py — the ONLY file changed this phase. Follows
  directly from a read-only performance audit (previous phase) that
  identified get_db_connection() opening a brand-new, un-pooled
  psycopg2 connection on every single call — measured empirically at
  ~34-141ms per connection open vs ~0.7ms to run a query on an already-
  open one — as the systemic root cause of slow page loads across the
  whole app (every route calls get_user_by_id(), which itself calls
  get_db_connection(), before doing any real work; several endpoints
  additionally loop and open many more connections per request).

  No query, matching, anomaly-detection, authenticity, AI Assistant,
  approval-assessment, or workflow logic was touched — this phase is
  connection handling ONLY, exactly as scoped.

  auditlens-backend/db.py:
    - get_db_connection() now borrows from a lazily-created
      psycopg2.pool.ThreadedConnectionPool instead of calling
      psycopg2.connect() directly. Same Config.DB_* environment
      variables, same connection kwargs, same function name/signature/
      return value (a live, connection-like object) as before — every
      existing caller (193 call sites across 32 files, none touched)
      keeps working unmodified.
    - New _PooledConnection(psycopg2.extensions.connection) subclass
      overrides ONLY close() — instead of tearing down the socket, it
      rolls back any open transaction defensively (so a route that
      raised mid-transaction can never leak dirty state into whichever
      request borrows this same connection next) and returns the
      connection to the pool. Every other method (cursor(), commit(),
      rollback(), etc.) is inherited unchanged from the real psycopg2
      connection class — this is what lets hundreds of existing
      "conn = get_db_connection(); ...; conn.close()" call sites keep
      behaving identically without being rewritten to call a pool's own
      putconn(). close() stays idempotent (safe to call twice, matching
      real psycopg2 behavior) and never lets a pool-bookkeeping edge
      case surface as a NEW error type to callers that only ever
      expected close() to succeed silently.
    - The pool is created LAZILY, on the first real get_db_connection()
      call — not at module import time — so importing db.py (e.g. from
      a test that fully monkey-patches get_db_connection() and never
      calls the real implementation) still never touches the network,
      matching the previous behavior exactly.
    - Pool sized conservatively (minconn=1, maxconn=10) based on
      inspecting Dockerfile (gunicorn --workers 2, no --threads
      configured — 2 worker PROCESSES, each importing db.py
      independently and getting its own pool, 1 request at a time per
      worker today) and render.yaml (a small/free-tier managed Postgres
      instance) — worst-case total physical connections stays well
      within a safe budget, with headroom if worker/thread config
      changes later.

Why:
  Direct continuation of the read-only performance audit's #1 finding:
  connection-open overhead (not query execution time, and not row
  count — every core table is currently empty) is what dominates page-
  load latency today, and will only get worse as N+1 query patterns
  (documented separately in the audit, deliberately NOT touched this
  phase) compound against real data volume later.

Confirmed unchanged (safety rules for this phase):
  - No business logic, audit rules, matching, anomaly detection,
    authenticity verification, AI Assistant, approval assessment, or
    workflow-timeline code touched — git diff --stat shows exactly one
    file, db.py, changed.
  - No API response format changes — every endpoint checked below
    returned the identical response shape it did before.
  - No database schema changes, no migration.
  - No DB_* environment variable behavior changed — the exact same
    Config.DB_NAME/DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD/DB_HOST/DB_PORT values already
    read before are still the only inputs to the pool's connection
    kwargs.
  - get_user_by_id() (also in db.py) required NO edit — it already
    calls get_db_connection() internally, so it benefits from pooling
    automatically.

Test results:
  - Full backend regression suite (python tests/extraction/run_all.py,
    all 26 suites, including 5 suites that exercise REAL database
    connections end-to-end — test_phase4_integration.py,
    test_shadow_comparison.py, test_transaction_auditor_integration.py,
    test_transaction_packages.py, test_relationship_builder.py) — all
    PASS, run twice (once immediately after the change, once again as
    a final gate right before committing) with identical results both
    times.
  - Direct smoke test of the pool mechanics themselves: confirmed
    importing db.py does not create the pool (lazy init preserved);
    first get_db_connection() call took ~39ms (pool creation + one real
    connection); a SECOND call reused the exact same underlying
    connection object in ~0.0ms; close() took ~0.5ms (rollback+return,
    not a real socket teardown); calling close() twice on the same
    connection did not raise (idempotence preserved); get_user_by_id()
    still round-trips correctly through the pool; 10 sequential
    borrow+query+close cycles averaged ~0.14ms/cycle (vs ~34-141ms/
    cycle for a fresh connection under the old implementation — roughly
    a 250-1000x reduction in connection-acquisition cost alone).
  - Live-verified against the real dev backend (throwaway auditor +
    finance_executive accounts, cleaned up afterward) with a
    deliberately-inserted, fully-disposable 2-invoice fixture (one
    clean PASS record with a matching PO+GR; one exception record with

    - Auditor Home / Review Queue: GET /auditor/transactions,

Date: 2026-07-27
What was changed:
  Fixed a real, previously-undetected bug in the login page's pipeline
  connector line: the animated indigo-to-purple dashed line above the
  6 pipeline icons was invisible in every browser, despite the two
  prior "fix" passes both showing the SVG's computed styles as
  correct (stroke correctly referencing the gradient, gradient stops
  correctly resolving to #6366f1/#a855f7). Root cause: the
  <linearGradient> used the SVG default gradientUnits="objectBoundingBox",
  and the <line> it painted (x1=20,y1=3 to x2=440,y2=3 - perfectly
  horizontal) has a bounding box with zero height. A bounding-box-
  relative gradient can't compute a valid transform against a
  zero-size dimension, so the browser silently painted nothing -
  the stroke reference and gradient stops were both technically
  "correct" (which is why prior getComputedStyle-based checks passed)
  but nothing ever actually reached the screen.
  - auditlens-frontend/src/app/login/login.component.html: the
    <linearGradient id="pipelineLineGrad"> gained
    gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse" and explicit x1="20" y1="3" x2="440"
    y2="3" coordinates (matching the <line>'s own endpoints in the
    SVG's viewBox space) instead of the default fractional 0-to-1
    objectBoundingBox coordinates. userSpaceOnUse maps the gradient
    directly onto the SVG's coordinate system rather than the shape's
    (degenerate) bounding box, sidestepping the zero-height issue
    entirely. No other change - same colors, same dasharray, same
    flowDash animation.

Why:
  User provided a fresh screenshot of the live (correctly-deployed,
  cache-confirmed-fresh) page and pointed out the connector line
  genuinely wasn't there - not a caching issue this time, an actual
  rendering bug. A closer investigation (zoomed screenshot at the
  exact pipeline-line region) confirmed zero visible line, prompting
  the objectBoundingBox/zero-height-bbox root-cause analysis above.

Confirmed unchanged (safety rules for this phase):
  - No backend file touched.
  - No login logic touched.
  - No other route, page, or shared component touched.
  - Every other element of the pipeline/capability/background work
    from the two prior passes re-verified unaffected by this change.

Test results:
  - npx ng build --configuration production - succeeded (exit 0; new
    main-*.js hash confirms the fix is actually captured in the
    build, same pre-existing bundle-size warnings as before).
  - Live-verified in a real browser (Playwright):
    - Zoomed, high-DPI screenshot of the exact connector-line region
      now shows a clearly visible dashed indigo-to-purple line running
      the full width above the 6 icons (previously: nothing visible
      in the same crop, confirmed by a before/after screenshot
      comparison at 2x device scale).
    - stroke-dashoffset sampled 3 times over 2 seconds
      (-13.33 / -29.60 / -5.60), confirming the flowDash animation is
      still actively running post-fix, not just statically visible.
  - Re-ran the full prior-phase regression suite (19 checks): 17/19

Date: 2026-08-02
What was changed:
  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/src/app/auditor/authenticity-detail/
  auditor-authenticity-detail.component.ts):
    - Added a new 'AUDITOR_CONFIRMED' EvidenceStatus value alongside the
      existing AI_DETECTED/AUDITOR_CORRECTED/AUDITOR_ADDED states, with
      its own label ("Auditor Confirmed"), and reused the existing
      green icon-yes styling.
    - AUDITOR_CORRECTED/AUDITOR_ADDED labels now read "... · Pending
      Re-check" - they now always mean "saved but not yet reconfirmed
      by an AI run", a state distinct from AUDITOR_CONFIRMED.
    - partyRows getter: a saved correction now resolves to
      AUDITOR_CONFIRMED (instead of staying AUDITOR_CORRECTED/
      AUDITOR_ADDED forever) once authenticity_checks.created_at is
      newer than the correction's corrected_at - i.e. an AI recheck has
      run since the correction was saved. The comparison is a pure
      frontend computation; the correction's own coordinates and the
      original_ai_box/corrected_by/corrected_at audit trail are
      untouched, so nothing about the corrections table's data changes
      - only how its age relative to the latest AI run is read.
    - actionFor() (decides whether an edit is logged as a "correction"
      vs a fresh "add") now also treats AUDITOR_CONFIRMED like
      AI_DETECTED/AUDITOR_CORRECTED, so re-editing an already-confirmed
      box keeps its correction lineage instead of being miscategorized
      as a brand-new addition.
    - No HTML/CSS changes needed: the existing
      [class.evidence-polygon-auditor]="status === 'AUDITOR_CORRECTED'
      || status === 'AUDITOR_ADDED'" binding already excludes any other
      status string, so AUDITOR_CONFIRMED falls through to the default
      green polygon styling for free.
  Backend (auditlens-backend/routes/authenticity.py):
    - _with_authentication_score() now explicitly calls .isoformat() on
      the row's created_at before it reaches jsonify(), matching the
      convention evidence_corrections.py already uses for corrected_at.
      This was a required bug fix, not a style change: Flask's default
      JSON encoder formats a raw (timezone-naive) datetime via HTTP's
      GMT-labelled RFC 1123 format WITHOUT converting the DB session's
      local wall-clock value to true UTC first - it just relabels those
      digits "GMT". Comparing that against evidence_corrections[].
      corrected_at (already isoformat()'d, no zone) on the frontend
      produced a spurious ~8 hour skew (this dev DB session runs in
      Asia/Kuala_Lumpur, UTC+8), which made a correction saved seconds
      ago look "confirmed" immediately, before any recheck had run.
      Normalizing both fields to the same bare-ISO convention fixes the
      comparison and, as a side effect, also fixes the "Checked: ..."
      timestamp already shown elsewhere on this page, which was
      silently off by the session's UTC offset before this change.

Why:
  User-requested workflow change: AI-detected boxes stay green: after
  an auditor edits/adds an evidence box it should show orange with
  "Auditor Corrected · Pending Re-check" until the auditor clicks
  Re-check Analysis, at which point - if the correction is still being
  shown - it should turn green and read "Auditor Confirmed", without
  the fresh AI results overwriting the auditor's saved coordinates, and
  without needing a manual page reload. Green now means "the current
  evidence location is confirmed", whether that confirmation came from
  the AI or from an auditor whose correction has survived a recheck.

Date: 2026-08-02
What was changed:
  Backend:
    - app.py: new anomaly_detection_runs table (auto-created at startup,
      same _ensure_*_table() pattern as every other table in this file)
      logging one row per actual detection run (invoice_document_id,
      anomalies_found, run_at) - the ONLY way to answer "when was this
      last screened" for a transaction that was screened and found
      clean, since a clean result inserts no row into `anomalies`.
    - helpers/anomaly_detector.py: added _log_detection_run(), called at
      both exit points of the existing, UNCHANGED run_anomaly_detection()
      (the "no anomalies found" early return and the normal end-of-run
      return) - detection logic, thresholds, and the anomalies table
      writes are untouched; this only adds a run-log side effect.
    - routes/anomalies.py: new POST /anomalies/run (auditor-only) - the
      backend behind the page's new "Run Anomaly Analysis" button. Loops
      over every invoice with extracted fields and re-runs the SAME
      delete-then-redetect pattern already used by routes/admin.py's
      single-document diagnostic endpoint and scripts/backfill_anomaly_
      detection.py, just across every invoice instead of one; one
      document failing is logged and skipped, never aborts the batch.
      GET /anomalies/stats gains 3 new fields - pending (status=
      'pending' count), transactions_analysed (COUNT(extracted_fields) -
      every invoice with extracted fields has gone through detection,
      since it's auto-triggered unconditionally right after extraction),
      last_analysed (MAX(run_at) from the new run-log table, explicitly
      .isoformat()'d before jsonify - Flask's default datetime encoder
      mislabels a naive DB timestamp as "GMT" without converting it,
      the same bug fixed in routes/authenticity.py last change).
      Existing fields (total, by_severity, by_type) and every existing
      route (list, review, stats' original shape) are unchanged - purely
      additive, and the two other pages that already read /anomalies/
      stats (auditor-dashboard, auditor-report) only read by_type/
      by_severity, so they're unaffected.

      Detected, Pending Review, Last Analysed) using the same KPI stat-
      card language already established on the Authenticity list page,
      reused here for visual consistency - all 4 values come straight
      from /anomalies/stats, nothing hard-coded.
    - New "Run Anomaly Analysis" button (same icon/text-swap loading
      pattern as the Authenticity Detail page's "Re-check Analysis"
      button): disables and shows "Running Analysis..." while POST
      /anomalies/run is in flight, then automatically re-calls the
      existing loadStats()/loadAnomalies() to refresh the page's data
      with no manual reload needed.
    - Type filter labels renamed (Amount -> Unusual Amount, Round ->
      Round Amount, Weekend -> Timing, Dup -> Duplicate) - only the
      AnomalyType union's `label` text changed; the `key` values (and

      values) are untouched.

      transaction has actually been screened, shows a dynamic message
      (transaction count and singular/plural pulled from the real
      transactions_analysed count, not hard-coded to "1") plus a
      Completed / Limited-by-insufficient-history checklist. Timing and
      round-amount checks (single-document signals) are always
      "Completed" once screening has happened; duplicate comparison
      is marked "limited" when transactions_analysed <= 1 (no other
      transaction exists to compare against) and unusual-amount
      analysis when transactions_analysed < 4 (helpers/anomaly_
      detector.py's detect_amount_anomaly needs >= 3 PRIOR same-vendor
      invoices - since one vendor's history can never exceed the
      system-wide total, a total below 4 guarantees insufficient
      history for every vendor, an honest lower bound rather than a
      guess). The "insufficient history" note/section only renders when
      at least one check is actually limited. The original two empty-
      state messages (a fresh system with zero screened transactions;
      anomalies exist but the current filters hide them all) are
      unchanged.
    - When anomalies exist: filter chips, severity, status, and the
      Investigate / Complete Review / False Positive actions are
      entirely unchanged - only the type filter LABELS changed, per the
      task's explicit "preserve" requirement.
    - Responsive: the summary bar uses an auto-fit grid (wraps to 2
      columns under 640px, 1 column under 420px) instead of a fixed
      column count; the header stacks the title and the new button
      vertically under 640px.

Why:
  User-requested improvement to the Auditor "Anomaly Detection" page:
  give auditors an at-a-glance analysis summary, a way to re-run
  detection on demand instead of only relying on the automatic per-
  upload trigger, a more honest/informative empty state for the common

What was changed:
