  finance/upload/finance-upload.component.ts/.html/.css, plus package.
  json/package-lock.json (new dependency: jszip) and angular.json (one
  line: allowedCommonJsDependencies: ["jszip"], to silence Angular's
  expected "not ESM" build warning for that package - purely cosmetic,
  no behavior change).
    - ZIP batch upload: .zip added to the file picker and accepted via
      drag-and-drop. A selected/dropped ZIP is extracted entirely
      client-side with JSZip - the ZIP itself is never uploaded or
      stored, only its supported entries (PDF/JPG/JPEG/PNG) are. Nested
      ZIPs, unreadable/encrypted entries, and unsupported formats are
      skipped with a note; directory entries, __MACOSX metadata, and
      dotfiles (.DS_Store, etc.) are ignored silently as routine ZIP
      noise. A ZIP whose own container is encrypted/corrupted fails to
      load entirely and reports one clear top-level error. Extracted
      entries over 10MB (the page's own already-documented "Maximum
      10MB per file" rule, not a new limit) are skipped. A ZIP that
      yields zero supported documents shows a clear "contains no
      supported documents" error. Same-name+same-size duplicates
      (against anything already staged or queued) are skipped; a
      previous FAILED entry with the same name+size is still replaced
      on re-add, matching this page's pre-existing retry-by-re-add
      behavior.
    - Document type recognition: every newly added/extracted file lands
      in a new "Confirm Document Types" staging list (NOT the upload
      queue) with a document type guessed from its filename - invoice/
      inv -> Invoice, purchase_order/purchase-order/po -> Purchase
      Order, goods_receipt/goods-receipt/gr -> Goods Receipt (word-
      boundary matched, so e.g. "report.pdf" doesn't false-positive on
      "po"), defaulting to Invoice otherwise. The type is shown in an
      editable dropdown per file; nothing uploads until the file is
      explicitly confirmed (per-file "Confirm" or a "Confirm All" for
      the whole batch) or removed. This is a purely frontend label -
      the actual backend document_type enum used elsewhere (e.g.
      authenticity_checks.document_type) is untouched.
    - Sequential processing + routing: confirmed files still upload one
      at a time through the SAME queue engine as before. Invoice-typed
      files upload via the existing (unchanged) POST /documents/upload.
      Purchase Order/Goods Receipt-typed files reuse the existing
      "attach to an invoice" endpoints (POST /documents/upload-po/<id>,
      POST /documents/upload-gr/<id>) - the target invoice is the one
      most recently uploaded earlier in the SAME batch (so a ZIP/multi-
      select containing an Invoice + PO + GR wires them together
      automatically), falling back to whatever document the user has
      separately selected via the page's existing "Attach PO/GR" flow.
      A Purchase Order/Goods Receipt with no available target invoice
      fails with a clear message rather than silently doing nothing -
      and does not stop the rest of the queue.
    - Upload/processing progress: switched from a plain observe:'body'
      POST to reportProgress:true, observe:'events', tracking real
      HttpEventType.UploadProgress ticks for the actual transfer
      percentage. IMPORTANT correction made during live testing:
      HttpEventType.Sent fires at the START of a request (right after
      it's dispatched), not after the upload finishes - confirmed live
      via direct console inspection of every event, which showed type=0
      (Sent) arriving BEFORE any UploadProgress events. The original
      implementation used Sent to trigger the "OCR and AI Processing"
      state, which made every file skip the uploading-percentage
      display entirely (verified live with a throttled connection:
      status jumped straight to "OCR and AI Processing" at t=0ms for
      every file, 0 distinct percentages ever observed). Fixed to
      switch to 'processing' when an UploadProgress event's own
      loaded reaches total instead - re-verified live over a CDP-
      throttled connection: 100 distinct percentage values observed
      climbing 0%->100%, THEN switching to "OCR and AI Processing" with
      the exact required message "OCR and AI extraction in progress.
      This may take a moment." (indeterminate, no fabricated
      percentage). Each queued row shows one of 5 states - Waiting /
      Uploading (with a live %) / OCR and AI Processing (indeterminate)
      / Completed / Failed - plus a new "Processing Summary" panel
      (Total Files / Completed / Processing / Failed / "Processing N of
      Total") computed live from the queue.
    - Also fixed as part of "disable accidental duplicate submission"
      (explicit UX requirement): the sequential engine's own re-entry
      point now no-ops if an upload is already active, closing a
      pre-existing gap where a drag-drop mid-upload (not blocked by the
      dropzone's disabled state, which only gates click/Browse) could
      have started a second, concurrent upload.
    - "Clear Done" relabeled "Clear Completed"; the drained-queue
      message now reads "Batch processing completed: N successful, M
      failed." (matching the requested format exactly) instead of the
      previous generic "All files uploaded successfully!" - this
      summarizes the WHOLE current queue (unchanged scope from the
      original code, which already worked this way), not just the
      files from the most recent confirm action.
    - Everything else on this page - the PO/GR "Attach" section, the
      Recent Upload Queue table, pagination, view/delete actions - is
      completely unchanged.

  documents in one action instead of selecting each file individually,

Date: 2026-08-03
What was changed:
  Backend (auditlens-backend/routes/anomalies.py):
    - get_anomaly_stats() (GET /anomalies/stats) rewritten to explicitly
      JOIN anomalies to documents on a.invoice_document_id = d.document_
      id for every count (total, by_severity, by_type, by_status) -
      anomalies has no document_id column of its own (the real FK is
      invoice_document_id), and this JOIN also naturally excludes an
      "orphan" anomaly row (invoice_document_id with no matching
      document) from every total instead of it silently inflating one.
    - transactions_analysed/last_analysed now come from anomaly_
      detection_runs (COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_document_id) + MAX(run_at)
      in one query) instead of a plain COUNT(*) FROM extracted_fields -
      the more accurate source, since it reflects actual detection runs
      rather than every extracted document regardless of whether
      detection ever ran on it.
    - That anomaly_detection_runs query is now isolated in its own try/
      except with conn.rollback() on failure (clears the aborted-
      transaction state Postgres leaves behind after a caught error, so
      the connection stays usable afterward) - an empty table already
      returns cleanly in plain SQL (COUNT 0, MAX NULL, no exception), but
      a missing/broken table no longer 500s the whole endpoint; either
      way it falls through to a fallback query: COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_
      document_id) from anomalies JOINed to documents (same orphan-
      exclusion join as above). last_analysed has no fallback source and
      stays None ("Never") when the runs table is unusable - only that
      table actually knows when detection last ran, so this stays honest
      rather than fabricating a timestamp.
  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/src/app/auditor/anomalies/):
    - auditor-anomalies.component.ts: loadStats()'s error handler
      previously did nothing, silently leaving the all-zero default

Date: 2026-08-03
What was changed:
  Root cause: app.py::_ensure_document_review_steps_table() (added in
  the previous entry) never called conn.close() on its except path -
  if the CREATE TABLE statement failed for any reason on Render's
  Postgres, that pooled connection (see db.py's _PooledConnection) was
  never returned to the pool, and the only trace was a WARNING line
  easy to miss in a full deploy log; the table's actual absence then
  only surfaced later, at request time, as "relation document_
  review_steps does not exist" from routes/reviews.py::mark_review_step.
  Backend (auditlens-backend/app.py):
    - _ensure_document_review_steps_table() rewritten: conn is now
      always closed via try/finally regardless of success or failure
      (fixes the connection-pool leak). The CREATE TABLE/INDEX
      statements themselves are unchanged (still CREATE ... IF NOT
      EXISTS - idempotent, touches no existing row on a boot where the
      table already exists) and still run in the same position in the
      startup sequence, before any blueprint's routes can be hit.
    - Added an explicit post-CREATE verification query (SELECT to_
      regclass('document_review_steps')) instead of assuming success
      just because no exception was raised - logs a clear, greppable
      "document_review_steps table ready (verified present)" line on
      success, or a loud ERROR line (naming DB user privileges/search_
      path as the likely cause) if the table still isn't visible for
      any other reason. The WARNING path on a genuine exception is
      unchanged in wording, just no longer leaks the connection.

Why:
  User-reported production error: "relation document_review_steps does
  not exist" when marking an Audit Review checklist step as reviewed,
  meaning the auto-create-on-startup migration added in the previous
  session's session did not actually create the table on Render. The
  connection leak above is the concrete bug found by inspection - a
  failed CREATE TABLE attempt (for whatever transient reason on that
  specific boot) would have left no clear diagnostic trail and could
  starve a later migration or request of a healthy pooled connection.
  The added verification step makes any FUTURE recurrence immediately
  visible in the Render deploy log instead of only surfacing minutes or
  hours later as a confusing "relation does not exist" at request time.

Date: 2026-08-03
What was changed:
  Root cause (confirmed by direct DB inspection, not assumed): every
  timestamp column in this schema is Postgres `timestamp without time
  zone` (naive), populated by server-side now()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  defaults. A naive column has no timezone metadata of its own - its
  stored digits are whatever the DB SESSION's timezone happened to be
  at insert time. This local dev machine's Postgres session defaults to
  Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (inherited from the OS), while Render's managed
  Postgres defaults to UTC - so the exact same code could silently
  store different wall-clock digits depending on environment. On top of
  that, every route read those naive values back out via a bare
  `.isoformat()` (or, worse, left a raw datetime for Flask's default
  JSON encoder, which formats it as an HTTP-style "Sun, 02 Aug 2026
  21:19:00 GMT" string) - neither carries a real timezone marker, so a
  browser's `new Date(...)` parses the string as LOCAL time instead of
  UTC, and every page's own hand-rolled toLocaleString()/
  toLocaleDateString() call (no explicit timeZone) just re-displayed
  those digits unconverted. Net effect: a UTC instant of 21:19 displayed
  as "21:19" instead of being shifted +8h to "05:19" the next day - the
  exact bug reported on Report & Log, and, by the same code paths,
  Review History, Workflow Timeline, review-step reviewed times,
  Anomaly timestamps/Last Analysed, and Approval/Send Back/Need Review
  records.

  Backend (auditlens-backend/):
    - db.py: the connection pool now passes `options='-c timezone=UTC'`
      to every pooled Postgres connection, on every environment. This is
      the root-cause fix - every now()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP write, from
      this point forward, consistently stores real UTC digits in these
      naive columns, regardless of the underlying Postgres instance's
      own OS/session default. (Render's managed Postgres was very
      likely already UTC-by-default, so this is mainly what makes local
      dev match production instead of silently diverging - not
      necessarily what caused the originally reported bug on its own.)
    - New helpers/time_format.py: `to_utc_iso(value)` turns a naive
      datetime into 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ' (explicit UTC marker); a
      plain date (or None) passes through unchanged, since a date-only
      value has no time-of-day to mark as UTC and must never gain one.
      `serialize_row_datetimes(row)` is the same row-wide, type-aware
      replacement for the `for k,v in row.items(): if hasattr(v,
      'isoformat'): row[k]=v.isoformat()` idiom repeated across routes/
      - real datetimes get the Z suffix, plain dates don't.
    - app.py: registered a custom Flask JSON provider (_UtcJSONProvider)
      as a catch-all - any raw datetime/date that reaches jsonify()
      without an explicit call now goes through the same to_utc_iso()/
      plain-isoformat() logic instead of the old GMT-labeled default.
    - Applied to_utc_iso()/serialize_row_datetimes() at every endpoint
      backing the reported pages: routes/auditor.py (_build_comparison's
      invoice uploaded_at - used by Workflow Timeline's "Document
      Uploaded" step; the /report/audit-trail timestamp), routes/
      ai_assistant.py (_build_case_context's audit_history reviewed_at
      and send_back_cycle sent_back_at - both feed Workflow Timeline
      event timestamps), routes/documents.py (the Workflow Timeline
      endpoint's review_steps[].reviewed_at), routes/anomalies.py
      (created_at and the Anomaly stats' last_analysed - invoice_date on
      the same rows is left untouched, still a plain date string),
      routes/reviews.py (mark_review_step's own response - the auditor
      clicking "Mark as Reviewed" updates the Review-step time on
      screen straight from THIS response, not a reload, so it needed
      the same fix; get_review_history's and get_send_back_cycles'
      generic loops, now via serialize_row_datetimes() - response_
      due_date on the latter stays a plain date, everything else on
      that row gets the Z suffix).
    - CSV export (/auditor/report/audit-trail/export.csv) was
      deliberately left untouched - a downloaded file for a spreadsheet
      is a different consumption context than the app's own display,
      and wasn't part of what was reported broken.

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/):
    - New shared/datetime.util.ts: the ONE shared formatter,
      formatMalaysiaDateTime(isoString), used by every page below
      instead of each writing its own toLocaleString()/
      toLocaleDateString() call. Parses the (now Z-suffixed) UTC string
      via `new Date(...)` and formats it through
      `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-MY', { timeZone: 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur', ...
      hour12: true })` - an EXPLICIT timezone conversion, not reliant on
      the viewer's own machine already being set to Malaysia time (what
      every removed toLocaleString() call implicitly assumed, and why
      the bug wasn't "8 hours off" for everyone testing on a
      Malaysia-timezone machine, only for whatever produced the
      originally reported screenshot). Confirmed empirically (Node's
      Intl, not assumed) that 'en-MY' already formats exactly as
      required with zero manual string assembly: new Date('2026-08-
      02T21:19:00Z') -> "03 Aug 2026, 05:19 am".
    - auditor-record-detail.component.ts's formatDateTime() (Review-step
      reviewed time, Review History, Send Back's "Finance Response"
      timestamp, the inline Document Workflow Timeline's "Document
      Uploaded" line) now delegates to the shared formatter instead of
      its own toLocaleString() call. formatDate() (Invoice Date,
      response_due_date - both date-only) is untouched.
    - workflow-timeline.component.ts's formatDate() (the shared
      Workflow Timeline component, used on both Auditor Record Detail's
      Finance Correction context and Finance Correction Detail) likewise
      delegates to the shared formatter.
    - auditor-report.component.ts's formatTimestamp() (Report & Log /
      Audit Trail) keeps its existing "relative time for today, absolute
      otherwise" behavior (untouched, and was never actually broken -
      Date.now() - new Date(ts).getTime() compares real instants
      correctly regardless of display timezone) but its absolute-
      fallback branch now calls the shared formatter instead of its own
      24-hour, no-year toLocaleDateString()+toLocaleTimeString() combo.
    - auditor-anomalies.component.ts's relativeTime() (Anomaly
      timestamps, Last Analysed) - same treatment: the "X min/hr/days
      ago" branches are untouched, only the 30+-day absolute fallback
      (previously date-only, no time at all) now calls the shared
      formatter. formatInvoiceDate() (date-only) is untouched.
    - Calendar (auditor/calendar) was not touched - it only ever
      displays date-only fields (YYYY-MM-DD, no time-of-day) via its own
      already-correct local-date parsing, confirmed by reading the
      component; it was never actually timezone-converting a real
      timestamp, so there was nothing broken there to fix.

Why:
  Report & Log was showing 02 Aug 21:19 for a record whose real UTC
  timestamp was 2026-08-02T21:19:00 - correct Malaysia time (UTC+8) is
  03 Aug 2026, 05:19 am. Traced to two compounding issues: (1) the
  backend never marked its timestamp strings as UTC (no 'Z'/offset), so
  a browser had no way to know they weren't already local time, and (2)
  every page wrote its own ad-hoc toLocaleString() call with no explicit
  timezone, silently relying on the viewer's own machine already being
  set to Malaysia time. Fixing this properly meant going all the way to
  the DB session/serialization layer (so "UTC in, UTC out" is
  guaranteed, not just patched per page) and consolidating every display
  call site onto one shared, explicitly-Malaysia-timezone formatter.

Build result:
  Backend: all 33 suites in tests/extraction/run_all.py pass (invoice/
  PO/GR extraction, authenticity, matching, anomalies, review steps,
  send-back, calendar - none of which this change's logic touches,
  confirming no regression), plus `python -c "import app"` clean.
  Frontend: `ng build --configuration development` and `ng build
  --configuration production` both clean (the production budget
  warnings printed are pre-existing bundle/CSS-size warnings unrelated
  to this change).

  Live verification against the real local dev stack (python app.py +
  ng serve, real Postgres, real login as vision_fixture_auditor@x.com):
  confirmed the DB session's `SHOW timezone` is now 'UTC' and NOW()
  returns true UTC digits (previously Asia/Kuala_Lumpur on this
  machine). Inserted document_review_steps.reviewed_at = '2026-08-02
  21:19:00' (the exact value from the bug report) for INV-NBI-2026-0017
  (document_id=3753) and hit GET /documents/3753/timeline directly:
  response was {"reviewed_at": "2026-08-02T21:19:00Z", ...} - confirmed
  ISO 8601 UTC with the Z suffix. Then in the actual browser: Record
  Detail's Review-step line rendered exactly "Reviewed by Vision
  Fixture Auditor - 03 Aug 2026, 05:19 am" - the exact required output
  for the exact required input. Inserted a matching review_records row
  and confirmed Review History showed the same "03 Aug 2026, 05:19 am".
  Confirmed Invoice Date on the same page still reads "11 Feb 2026" -
  unshifted, unaffected, exactly its raw stored date value. Confirmed
  Report & Log's Audit Trail still shows "just now"/"X min ago" for
  today's entries (correct - the relative-time math was never actually
  broken once the underlying timestamp is properly UTC-tagged). All

Date: 2026-08-03
What was changed:
  Follow-up to the previous commit (fix: standardize Malaysia timezone
  display), which fixed individual timestamp DISPLAY but not day-level
  GROUPING. Root cause (confirmed by direct Postgres query, not
  assumed): `DATE(some_naive_utc_column)` and `TO_CHAR(..., 'YYYY-MM')`
  extract the calendar unit directly from the column's raw UTC digits -
  correct for "what UTC date/month is this", wrong for "what Malaysia
  date/month is this", which is what every chart/trend/"today" concept
  in this app actually means. A review at 21:19 UTC (05:19 the next
  Malaysia morning) was landing in the PREVIOUS UTC day's bucket, so any
  chart's rightmost/most-recent bucket could lag Malaysia's real "today"
  by up to a day. Investigated the actual architecture behind every
  named Auditor and Finance area before touching anything: Auditor's
  charts (Dashboard Audit Trend, Review Volume, Report & Log's own
  trend) all trace to ONE backend endpoint (/auditor/report/summary)
  that already SQL-day-buckets server-side; Finance's charts (Home's
  Upload Trend + 5 other "this month"-scoped charts) have NO backend
  aggregation at all - every Finance page fetches raw, un-aggregated
  document/package lists and buckets them client-side in TypeScript, an
  architecture confirmed by grep across the entire finance/ directory,
  not assumed. Given that split, and after presenting the tradeoff to
  the user (build new backend aggregation endpoints for Finance to
  literally match "one shared backend helper", vs. keep Finance's
  existing frontend-grouping architecture but make it explicitly
  Malaysia-aware instead of implicitly browser-local), the user chose
  the smaller, lower-risk frontend fix for Finance - so this commit is
  a backend fix for Auditor and a frontend fix for Finance, each
  reusing exactly one new shared helper on its own side.

  Backend (auditlens-backend/) - Auditor only, nothing here touches
  Finance's endpoints since none of them aggregate by date server-side:
    - helpers/time_format.py gained 4 new shared functions alongside
      the existing UTC-Z display helpers: malaysia_today() (today's
      real Asia/Kuala_Lumpur calendar date, computed from the current
      UTC instant - not server-local time, which could be any timezone
      depending on where the process happens to run), to_malaysia_date()
      (Python-side: naive UTC datetime -> its Malaysia calendar date),
      malaysia_midnight_utc() (Malaysia local midnight on a given date,
      converted to the naive UTC datetime needed as a WHERE-clause
      bound - Malaysia midnight is 16:00 UTC the PREVIOUS day), and
      malaysia_date_sql() (a SQL fragment - `(col AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT
      TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur')::date` - the one shared way every
      day-bucketed query must GROUP BY, instead of Postgres's own
      DATE(...)). Requires the zoneinfo stdlib module's IANA database;
      added tzdata==2026.3 to requirements.txt since Windows (unlike
      Render's Linux container) doesn't ship it and zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(
      'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur') would otherwise raise ZoneInfoNotFoundError
      on a dev machine - confirmed by hitting exactly that error first,
      not assumed.
    - routes/auditor.py: _period_start('today') (drives Report & Log's
      Approved/Sent Back/Pending/Exceptions KPI cards when the "Today"
      filter is active) now returns malaysia_midnight_utc(malaysia_
      today()) instead of datetime.utcnow().replace(hour=0,...) - the
      old version started "today" at UTC midnight, up to 8 hours before
      Malaysia's actual midnight. ('week'/'month' were left as rolling
      windows from real "now" - subtracting a fixed duration from now()
      gives the same instant regardless of which timezone "now" is
      expressed in, so there was nothing to fix there.)
    - get_report_summary()'s 30-day timeline (backs Dashboard Audit
      Trend, Review Volume, and Report & Log's Audit Activity Trend -
      confirmed to be the exact same endpoint/response, not 3 separate
      implementations) now anchors its 30-day window on malaysia_today()
      instead of datetime.utcnow(), and its two GROUP BY DATE(...)
      queries (review_records.reviewed_at, documents.uploaded_at) now
      GROUP BY malaysia_date_sql(...) instead - so the timeline's last
      bucket is always Malaysia's real "today", and each day's counts
      reflect what actually happened during that Malaysia calendar day.
    - _audit_trail_query()'s start_date/end_date (the Audit Trail
      date-range picker) arrive as plain 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings meaning
      whole Malaysia calendar days; comparing them directly against the
      naive-UTC reviewed_at column implicitly treated them as UTC
      midnight, silently dropping the first ~8 Malaysia-morning hours of
      start_date and cutting end_date off ~8 hours before Malaysia's own
      end of day. Now converted through malaysia_midnight_utc() - the
      end bound uses the FOLLOWING day's Malaysia midnight as an
      exclusive upper bound, so the selected end_date's entire Malaysia
      calendar day is included, not just up to its own midnight.

  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/) - Finance only:
    - shared/datetime.util.ts gained 3 new functions alongside the
      existing formatMalaysiaDateTime(): toMalaysiaDateKey() (UTC
      ISO string/Date -> 'YYYY-MM-DD' in Asia/Kuala_Lumpur, via
      Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur' }) -
      confirmed empirically, not assumed, that 'en-CA' formats as plain
      YYYY-MM-DD with no locale-punctuation surprises), isSameMalaysiaMonth()
      (compares two values' Malaysia year+month), and malaysiaMonthIndex()
      (0-based Malaysia month index, for a direct `months[...]` lookup).
    - finance-home.component.ts: replaced all 6 call sites that computed
      "this month"/a chart's month bucket via `new Date(x).getMonth()`/
      `.getFullYear()` (which use whichever timezone the VIEWER's own
      machine happens to be set to - only "correct" by coincidence for a
      viewer whose machine is already on Malaysia time, exactly the same
      class of bug the previous commit fixed for individual timestamp
      display) with the new shared helpers: loadDocuments()'s
      thisMonthDocs filter (feeds the KPI cards, Document Status
      Overview, Priority Finance Action panel), computeDocumentTypeDistribution(),
      computeCorrectionAnalysis(), renderUploadTrendChart()'s month
      bucketing, renderOcrPerfChart(), and renderOcrConfidenceChart().
      finance-report.component.ts/finance-transactions.component.ts/
      finance-corrections.component.ts were checked and confirmed to
      have no date/month-comparison logic of their own (grep across the
      whole finance/ directory found zero other getMonth()/getFullYear()/
      getDate() call sites) - their charts are purely categorical
      (status/vendor/match breakdowns), nothing to fix there.
    - Date-only business fields untouched throughout: grepped the full
      diff for invoice_date/po_date/receipt_date/response_due_date/
      gr_date and confirmed zero matches.

Why:
  Individual timestamps already displayed correctly in Asia/Kuala_Lumpur
  (the previous commit's fix), but charts and daily summaries were still
  grouping by the raw UTC calendar date/month underneath - so a chart
  could visibly end "yesterday" by Malaysia's clock even though every
  individual timestamp on the same page was already showing the right
  Malaysia time. Fixing this required converting to Asia/Kuala_Lumpur
  BEFORE extracting the calendar unit used for grouping, not just before
  display - a distinct bug class from the previous commit, worth its own
  shared helper.

Date: 2026-08-03
What was changed:
  Backend (auditlens-backend/):
    - app.py: new _ensure_document_hash_columns() (same auto-migration
      pattern as every other _ensure_* function) adds a
      sha256_baseline VARCHAR(64) column to documents/purchase_orders/
      goods_receipts. Matching migrations/2026-08-03_add_sha256_
      baseline.sql kept for local dev / documentation parity
      (gitignored, like every other *.sql in migrations/ - the auto-
      migration in app.py is what actually runs on Render).
    - routes/documents.py: the 3 upload routes (upload_document,
      upload-po, upload-gr) now persist the SHA-256 hash each of them
      was ALREADY computing (for AI-cache keying) as this new
      sha256_baseline column - no new hashing added, just no longer
      thrown away. New _compute_document_integrity(cursor, comparison)
      recomputes each present document's hash from its stored
      file_bytes and compares against that baseline: matches ->
      'verified', mismatch -> 'warning', no baseline or bytes
      unavailable -> 'not_recorded' (never a false 'verified'). Two new
      read-only GET routes (auditor/admin only, same role-gate as the
      comparison endpoint): /documents/<id>/integrity (used by the new
      Record Detail card) and /documents/<id>/evidence-passport (the
      full aggregation for the new page below - built entirely from
      existing helpers: _build_case_context, build_comparison,
      get_transaction_context_for_document, the same document_review_
      steps/send_back_cycles queries the Timeline/Send-Back-History
      endpoints already use - no matching/anomaly/authenticity/review-
      step logic duplicated or changed).
  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/):
    - New "Audit Evidence Passport" card on Audit Review (Record
      Detail), directly below the Document Workflow Timeline card (NOT
      inside it - no timeline dot, no lock, no Mark as Reviewed, no
      effect on canApprove/allMandatoryStepsReviewed gating). Shows
      Status (Draft/Finalised/Correction Required/Further Review,
      mapped from the SAME latestReviewAction caseFinalDecision already
      reads) and Document Integrity (Verified/Warning/Not Yet Recorded,
      from the new /integrity endpoint), with [View Evidence Passport]
      and [Export PDF] buttons.
    - New page at /auditor/evidence-passport/:document_id
      (AuditorEvidencePassportComponent, same standalone-component/
      Router-ActivatedRoute-HttpClient-getHeaders() shape as
      auditor-matching-details) - one read-only summary of a single
      transaction: transaction summary, invoice/PO/GR info, document
      integrity + SHA-256 status, OCR confidence, three-way matching
      result, exception findings, authenticity findings, anomaly
      findings, auditor review steps (reviewer/time), correction/
      resubmission history, final decision/remark/auditor/time, audit
      activity timeline. "Back to Audit Review" top-right.
    - Export PDF: this repo had no existing PDF-generation pattern (only
      a disabled "Coming soon" button on the Report page, no jsPDF/
      reportlab/etc. anywhere) - confirmed with the user before
      building anything. Implemented as browser print-to-PDF instead:
      an Export PDF button (both on the card and on the Passport page
      itself) calls window.print(), and the page has a @media print
      stylesheet that hides nav/buttons and paginates the summary
      sections cleanly. Reaching the page via the card's Export PDF
      button (?export=1) auto-triggers window.print() once the data
      has loaded. Zero new dependencies.
    - app.routes.ts: one new child route, same place as the existing
      authenticity/:documentId path-param page in this layout.

Why:
  Auditors currently have to visit several separate pages (Record
  Detail, Matching Details, Authenticity Detail, Anomaly Detail, review
  history) to piece together one transaction's full audit trail. The
  Evidence Passport gives them one read-only, exportable summary of
  everything already known about a transaction, plus a genuinely new
  piece of assurance - document integrity - that didn't exist before:
  proof (or an honest "not yet recorded") that a document's bytes still
  match what was uploaded, without ever claiming a false "Verified".

Verified:
  python tests/extraction/test_document_hash_integrity.py (new test,
  real local Postgres, all cases pass): migration adds sha256_baseline
  to all 3 tables and is idempotent (checked without ever DROPping the
  column - unlike the reference migration test this one didn't want to
  destructively wipe real baselines already on shared business tables
  in this dev DB); a document whose recomputed hash matches its
  baseline reads 'verified'; a tampered document reads 'warning', never
  'verified'; a document with no recorded baseline reads 'not_recorded',
  never a false 'verified'. python -c "import app" - clean import, new
  migration and both new routes register without error. npx ng build
  --configuration production - clean compile, only the same pre-
  existing bundle-budget warnings as before (record-detail.css grew by
  the new card's styles, already over budget beforehand). Did not run
  the full backend suite or Playwright, per this task's own scope.

Setup/config needed:
  1. Push to GitHub - Render should auto-deploy both the backend
     (Docker web service) and the frontend static site.
  2. Backend redeploy required (app.py, routes/documents.py changed) -
     on first boot after deploy, check the Render logs for "Document
     hash baseline columns ready" to confirm the migration applied.
  3. No new environment variables, no new dependencies. Existing
     documents/purchase_orders/goods_receipts rows keep
     sha256_baseline = NULL (Document Integrity reads "Not Yet
     Recorded" for them, by design - never backfilled, since a baseline
     recorded after the fact wouldn't prove anything) until each is
     next re-uploaded.

Date: 2026-08-03
What was changed:
  Backend (auditlens-backend/routes/reviews.py only):
    - Root cause found: finance_report()'s overall_status came from
      LEFT JOIN record_matches rm ON ef.extraction_id = rm.extraction_id
      - but record_matches is a DEAD table. Nothing in the current
        codebase inserts into it anymore; routes/matching.py's
        run_matching() (the only write path left with that name) writes
        to a DIFFERENT table, three_way_matches. So overall_status was
        NULL for every single document regardless of whether PO/GR were
        uploaded, and the frontend's old fallback logic misread every
        one of those NULLs as "Missing Documents" - even when Related
        Documents clearly showed both PO and GR linked.
    - Fix: dropped the dead record_matches join entirely. overall_status
      is now computed per document via build_comparison()/
      _matching_status_for_comparison() (routes/auditor.py) - the exact
      same live matching engine Record Detail, Matching Details, the
      Evidence Passport, and the Auditor queue's own standalone-invoice
      rows already trust - returning 'PASS'/'REVIEW'/'PARTIAL'/'FAIL',
      or 'PENDING' when no comparison exists yet. No new matching logic
      (calls the existing engine), no new endpoint. Runs once per
      document in this one Finance user's own upload list.
  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/.../finance/report/finance-report.component.ts only):
    - getMatchStatusLabel()/getMatchStatusClass() rewritten as a
      two-step check: hasBothSupportingDocs() (purchase_order_number
      AND goods_receipt_number both present - the real linkage already
      added to this endpoint) decides "Missing Documents" FIRST,
      independent of overall_status; only once both documents are
      genuinely present does overall_status decide Full Match (PASS) /
      Review Required (REVIEW or PARTIAL) / Mismatch (FAIL) / Pending
      (anything else, e.g. PENDING or an unrecognized value) - so an
      unknown/null status on a document that DOES have both documents
      linked now reads "Pending", never "Missing Documents".

Why:
  Reported bug: almost every package showed "Missing Documents" even
  when Related Documents clearly contained both PO and GR - traced to
  the query silently reading a table nothing writes to anymore, and a
  frontend fallback that couldn't tell "no status" apart from "no
  documents".

What was changed:
  Backend (auditlens-backend/routes/documents.py):
    - Root cause found: get_po_list() (GET /documents/po/list) returned
      EVERY PO belonging to the finance user, with no status filter at
      all. A PO has no reviewable status of its own — its OCR Review
      visibility is meant to be derived from its parent invoice's
      status, the same way GR's list already worked — but unlike GR,
      whose frontend (loadGRList()) was already filtering client-side
      to only invoices still 'ocr_done', PO had no equivalent filter
      anywhere, backend or frontend. So once an invoice was submitted
      (status -> 'under_review'), its GR correctly vanished from the
      queue on next load, but its PO stayed forever.
    - Fix: get_po_list() now accepts an opt-in ?pending_review=1 query
      param. When present, the SQL adds AND d.status = 'ocr_done' (the
      exact same "still requiring OCR review" definition the Invoice
      tab's own loadDocuments() already uses). Deliberately NOT an
      unconditional filter: finance-home.component.ts and finance-
      upload.component.ts also call this SAME endpoint and need POs for
      invoices in EVERY status — confirmed by reading finance-home.
      component.ts, whose "Missing PO" correction-analysis check
      specifically inspects RETURNED invoices (poDocumentIds.has(...)),
      and finance-upload.component.ts's own Related Documents column
      for already-approved/under-review packages. An unconditional
      filter would have silently broken both. The default (no query
      param) behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.

  review.component.ts):
    - loadPOList() now requests ?pending_review=1, so the PO tab shows

      unchanged.

Date: 2026-08-04
What was changed:
  Frontend only (auditlens-frontend/.../finance/upload/finance-upload.
  component.ts/.html/.css) - no backend touched.
    - inferDocType() rewritten: Goods Receipt is now checked BEFORE
      Purchase Order (previously PO was checked first), and its pattern
      now recognises GR, GRPO, GRN, "Goods Receipt", "Goods Receipt PO",
      and "Goods Received Note" - not just bare "gr". Root cause of the
      reported bug: "GRPO" satisfied neither the old PO regex (its "po"
      substring has no word-boundary before it, preceded by "r") nor
      the old GR regex (its "gr" substring has no word-boundary after
      it, followed by "po") - so it silently fell through to the
      Invoice default. Added an explicit Invoice/INV pattern as the
      3rd-priority check.
    - Unknown filenames (matching none of the 3 patterns) are now typed
      'unconfirmed' instead of defaulting to Invoice - a new StagedDocType
      = DocType | 'unconfirmed', used only by StagedFile (pre-
      confirmation); QueueItem/the actual upload pipeline still only
      ever sees a real DocType. confirmStaged()/confirmAllStaged() now
      refuse to move an 'unconfirmed' item into uploadQueue - Confirm
      All queues whatever IS confirmed and leaves the rest staged with
      a message; the per-row Confirm button is disabled while
      unconfirmed. The "Confirm Document Types" select shows an
      "Unconfirmed - select a type" placeholder option (disabled/
      hidden, so it can't be re-selected once changed) with a small red
      note under it.
    - uploadNextInQueue() now picks the next 'pending' item to actually
      process by document-type priority (Invoice -> Purchase Order ->
      Goods Receipt), not array/archive-entry order - a stable sort
      (ES2019+) over the pending items, so same-type items keep their
      original relative order. This is the ACTUAL fix for "ZIP
      processing depends on archive file order" - previously the queue
      just took the first 'pending' item in array order, which could be
      a PO or GR added earlier in a ZIP's own internal listing, before
      that batch's Invoice had even been attempted. The one-item-at-a-
      time sequential upload itself (unchanged) already guaranteed the
      Invoice's own HTTP call fully completes and returns document_id
      before anything else starts; this fix is entirely about WHICH
      pending item gets picked next, not the sequential-processing
      mechanism itself.
    - Same priority-based selection automatically makes retryFailed()
      (unchanged itself - it just flips failed items back to 'pending'
      in place) reprocess a batch's Invoice before its PO/GR on retry,
      with no separate retry-ordering code needed.
    - When a PO/GR has no invoice document_id to attach to, the error
      message now distinguishes two cases: if this batch's own Invoice
      item is present and its status is 'error', shows the exact
      required "Invoice upload must complete before supporting
      documents can be attached." (retrying is the actual fix); every
      other case (no Invoice was ever part of this batch) keeps the
      existing, more general "No invoice available..." guidance.
      Marked 'error' (the existing status value) rather than adding a
      new one.

Why:
  Reported bugs: a real filename ("NICEPACK - GRPO PD6012343.pdf") was
  being classified as Invoice instead of Goods Receipt, and because ZIP
  processing just walked the upload queue in whatever order files ended
  up in it (itself following the ZIP archive's own internal entry
  order), a Purchase Order could be attempted before its batch's own
  Invoice existed yet to attach to.

  against the new regex (NICEPACK - INV NP2606-0613.pdf -> Invoice,
  NICEPACK - PO 3006490.pdf -> Purchase Order, NICEPACK - GRPO
  PD6012343.pdf -> Goods Receipt; GR/GRN/"Goods Receipt"/"Goods Receipt
  PO"/"Goods Received Note" variants all -> Goods Receipt; a filename
  matching none of the 3 -> 'unconfirmed', never a default). npx ng

Date: 2026-08-04
What was changed:
  Backend (auditlens-backend/routes/auditor.py::_match_line_items(),
  the one shared line-item matcher both the legacy and V2/enterprise
  comparison paths already call - no separate implementation to fix
  twice):
    - Investigation: the reported transaction (item_code 7550011)
      doesn't exist in the local dev DB, so worked from the exact
      values given. Checked routes/documents.py's _sanitize_line_items(
      )/_save_line_items() (the extraction-to-DB mapping) and confirmed
      unit_price and amount are NOT swapped there - item['unit_price']
      maps to the unit_price column, item['amount'] to the amount
      column, correctly ordered. Requirement 5 satisfied by
      verification, no code change needed at that layer.
    - Root cause: unit_price was never compared at all - only amount
      (Line Amount) was, and only ONE conflated boolean drove the
      frontend's single "Amount/unit price differs" note, which could
      never distinguish a real price problem from a real amount
      problem. Added a SEPARATE unit_price_match, computed with the
      exact same float-with-tolerance comparison amount_match already
      used (abs(a - b) < 0.01) - so 0.6300 and 0.63000 (the same value,
      different stored precision) are correctly treated as equal, never
      compared as formatted strings. A document that carries no price
      at all for a line (a GR normally has neither unit_price nor
      amount) is simply excluded from that comparison's value list, the
      same way a missing quantity already was - the result stays None
      ("not compared") rather than ever being scored as a mismatch.
    - Also now exposes the raw per-side invoice_unit_price/po_unit_
      price/gr_unit_price and invoice_amount/po_amount/gr_amount
      (mirroring the existing invoice_quantity/po_quantity/gr_quantity
      fields), so the frontend can show the actual compared numbers,
      not just a pass/fail icon.
    - unit_price_match is a SOFT signal (has_soft_mismatch), same
      severity tier amount_match already was - unchanged escalation
      behaviour, just one more independent contributor to it.
  Frontend (auditlens-frontend/.../auditor/matching-details/):
    - The single "Amount/unit price differs" note (driven only by
      amount_match, so it could show even when the ACTUAL problem was a
      price difference or vice versa) replaced with two separate notes:
      "Unit price differs" (li.unit_price_match === false) and "Line
      amount differs" (li.amount_match === false) - each renders only
      when THAT specific comparison is an explicit false, never for
      None ("not compared"/N/A, e.g. GR's missing price), satisfying
      "show separate results" and "do not compare missing GR price/
      amount" together.
    - lineItemRowClass() now also flags unit_price_match === false
      (previously only amount_match). Kept the EXISTING partial-
      allocation exemption on amount_match only (a partially-allocated
      invoice legitimately totals less than the PO's full line, by
      design) - deliberately NOT applied to unit_price_match, since the
      per-unit rate should match regardless of how much quantity was
      allocated; a genuine per-unit price difference is still always
      worth flagging.
    - Description fuzzy matching (_find_line_item_match, the sole-line-
      item fallback) is untouched - confirmed by reading the full
      _match_line_items() body before editing, only the amount/
      unit_price block was touched.

Why:
  Reported bug: a real transaction (Invoice/PO both item_code 7550011,
  qty 3000, unit_price 0.63 stored at different precision, line total
  1890.00 on both sides, GR carrying no price data at all) showed
  "Amount/unit price differs" despite the numbers genuinely matching -
  traced to unit_price never being compared as its own signal, only
  folded (incompletely) into a single ambiguous note.

      Invoice qty=3000/unit_price=0.63/amount=1890.0, PO qty=3000/
      unit_price=0.63/amount=1890.0, GR qty=3000/unit_price=None/
      amount=3000.0 (GR's amount field wrongly held its own quantity).
      Confirms amount_match now comes out True (GR's bogus amount is
      excluded) while gr_amount is still exposed raw for display.

  auditor-matching-details.component.html/.css:
    - Each line item row now always displays the compared raw values
      when both Invoice and PO amounts are present: "Invoice Line
      Amount: RM x · PO Line Amount: RM y · Result: Match/Mismatch",
      reusing the existing formatAmount() helper. New .li-amount-compare
      CSS class (neutral/secondary text, green "Match", amber
      "Mismatch").

Why:
  Reported bug: after the previous unit-price/amount-split fix, a real
  production transaction (NICEPACK, invoice NP2606-0613, PO 3006490)
  still showed "Line amount differs" even though Invoice and PO
  genuinely matched (3000 x 0.63 = 1890.00 on both sides). User
  supplied the real stored document_line_items rows via a read-only
  query. Root cause: GR's `amount` column held 3000.0 - the same as
  GR's own quantity, an extraction artifact - while GR's `unit_price`
  was correctly NULL (GRs don't carry pricing). Because the comparison
  only excluded a value via `is not None`, GR's bogus 3000.0 got
  compared against Invoice/PO's correct 1890.0 and produced a false
  mismatch. Fix is comparison-side only (amount requires unit_price to
  be trusted) - no database write, no re-upload, no duplicate package;
  since build_comparison() computes live on every page view, the fix
  takes effect on the very next view of this transaction.

  tests/extraction/test_entity_and_line_items.py ("the relevant
  matching check", per this task's own scope) - all prior cases still
  pass unchanged, plus the new NICEPACK case confirms amount_match is

What changed:

  routes/authenticity.py:

2026-08-04

What changed:
  fix: display authenticity checked time in Malaysia timezone

  routes/authenticity.py:
    - _finish_authentication_score() now serializes
      authenticity_checks.created_at via helpers/time_format.py's
      to_utc_iso() (appends 'Z') instead of a bare .isoformat() call, so
      the frontend can tell this value is UTC instead of guessing.

  auditor-authenticity-detail.component.ts/.html:
    - The "Checked" technical-metadata timestamp now goes through the
      shared formatMalaysiaDateTime() utility (via a new formatDateTime()
      wrapper, matching the same pattern already used by auditor-record-
      detail.component.ts/auditor-anomalies.component.ts) instead of
      Angular's built-in `date:'medium'` pipe, which used the browser's
      own local timezone with no explicit Asia/Kuala_Lumpur conversion.
      This is the SAME created_at field shown both for the initial check
      and after Re-check Analysis (it's refreshed to NOW() on every AI
      run), so both are covered by this one fix.
    - isCorrectionConfirmed() now explicitly coerces both compared
      timestamps (created_at, evidence_corrections[].corrected_at) to be
      parsed as UTC (appending 'Z' if missing) before comparing, instead
      of relying on both happening to lack a timezone marker in the same
      way. Necessary companion fix: once created_at gained an explicit
      'Z' but corrected_at didn't, the two would have been parsed under
      different timezone assumptions, which could flip this comparison's
      result for a correction and a re-check that happen close together
      in time — the exact "Auditor Corrected -> Auditor Confirmed"
      transition fixed in the previous change on this page.
    - check.document_date (Invoice/PO/GR business date, shown at the top
      of the page) is untouched — still its own `| date:'mediumDate'`
      pipe, since it carries no time-of-day to convert.

Why:
  "Checked" was showing raw UTC digits unconverted (04 Aug 2026, 12:33
  pm instead of the correct 04 Aug 2026, 08:33 pm Malaysia time) —
  authenticity_checks.created_at was serialized as a bare, timezone-less
  ISO string, and the template used Angular's date pipe with no explicit
  timeZone, so display correctness depended entirely on the viewer's own
  machine already being set to Malaysia time.

  same pre-existing bundle-budget warnings on files this task never
  touched. python -c "import app" - clean import (not a test run). Did
  not run backend tests or Playwright, per this task's explicit
  instruction. git diff --stat confirms only routes/authenticity.py and
  the Authenticity Detail component's .ts/.html changed - no other
  page, no document business date, no unrelated timestamp field.

  1. Push to GitHub - Render should auto-deploy both the backend

  2. Backend + frontend redeploy required - no new migration, no new
     dependency, no new environment variable.
